# Phase 1 — Winter Program (Max Strength & Hypertrophy)

*September 20, 2026 · Kenneth Quinones, Assistant Football Coach LB/RB, Dover High School*

## Overview

Dates, anchored to Dover Public Schools' confirmed 2026-2027 district calendar: Testing Week (Week 1) runs **Monday, December 14 - Friday, December 18, 2026**, timed to land after Phase 0's post-season window and before Winter Break, so athletes aren't testing maxes right up against an 8-day closure (Winter Break itself carries no scheduled training week). Weeks 2-9 (8 training weeks) then run as follows:

| Week | Dates | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Winter Break | Dec 21, 2026 - Jan 3, 2027 | No formal training. District closure Dec 24-31 (an eight-day calendar entry; with Jan 1 that is nine consecutive closure dates, and school resumes Jan 4), plus the preceding week (Dec 21-23, capped by a single-session day Dec 23) isn't worth salvaging as a token training week - folded into the same break rather than run as a partial Week 2. |
| Week 2 | Jan 4-8, 2027 | First week back - see the transition-period note below. |
| Week 3 | Jan 11-15, 2027 | — |
| Week 4 | Jan 18-22, 2027 | MLK Day (Mon Jan 18) is a district closure - lands on this phase's already-scheduled volume-dip week (3 sets instead of 4, see Progression Scheme), so the single missed day is absorbed by an already-lighter week rather than needing special handling. |
| Week 5 | Jan 25-29, 2027 | — |
| Week 6 | Feb 1-5, 2027 | Retest week. |
| Week 7 | Feb 8-12, 2027 | **Staff In-Service - No School For Students (Mon Feb 8).** Unlike Weeks 4/8, Week 7 isn't a scheduled volume-dip week, so the missed Monday isn't already absorbed by lighter programming the way MLK Day and Presidents' Day are. Fix: **Day A (Back Squat) moves to Wednesday, Feb 10, this week only** - the template's normal open day for this phase - so the squad still gets all 4 sessions; Day B/C/D stay on their usual Tue/Thu/Fri. |
| Week 8 | Feb 15-19, 2027 | Presidents' Day (Mon Feb 15) is a district closure - same alignment as Week 4: lands on the other scheduled volume-dip week. |
| Week 9 | Feb 22-26, 2027 | Closes Phase 1. |

Phase 1 runs mid-December through late February - the calendar Phase 2 starts from (see that document's Overview).

## Pre-Testing Prep Sessions (Optional, Nov 10 - Dec 10, 2026)

Phase 0 now runs from the Monday after the roster's actual final game through the Sunday before this Testing Week - 6 or 7 whole calendar weeks in 2026, depending on the actual final-game date (the gap from the final game itself to Testing Week is roughly 6.4-7.4 weeks, since the game falls partway through its week). The first 1-2 weeks stay true active recovery (nothing programmed). What follows is a real, coach-facilitated, attendance-optional program for the remaining weeks - 9 sessions, Tuesday/Thursday, anchored to Dover's actual November-December calendar (Thanksgiving Break Nov 26-27 cuts one session). Attendance doesn't factor into roster status or playing time - it's voluntary the same way Phase 3's own pre-Testing-Window acclimation sessions are - but it's a real, programmed session a coach runs, not a handout athletes are left to interpret alone.

Barbell work during these sessions stays light technique re-familiarization only, never past RPE 5-6 (Rating of Perceived Exertion, a 1-10 effort scale where 10 is max effort and 5-6 is moderate with several reps left in the tank) - never a tested max.

**Format for every session: ~30-35 minutes, NMT warm-up first (same protocol as Phase 1's NMT warm-up, including the neck block) - this doubles as re-establishing the injury-prevention habit before Phase 1 proper starts.**

| Week | Sessions | Focus | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tue Nov 10, Thu Nov 12 | General reactivation | NMT warm-up. Bodyweight circuit, 2-3 rounds: goblet-hold bodyweight squat, push-up, bodyweight row (or band pull-apart), bodyweight RDL reach, plank variation. No barbell. Finish with 10-12 min easy-paced conditioning (jog, bike, or sled push at a conversational effort) - general work capacity, not interval training. |
| 2 | Tue Nov 17, Thu Nov 19 | Movement re-familiarization | NMT warm-up. Same bodyweight circuit, then introduce the empty bar (or a bar-only load, ~45 lb): 2x5 back squat, 2x5 bench press, technique-only, RPE 3-4 - a coach's chance to see who needs a technique refresher before real loading resumes in Testing Week. Light conditioning continues (10 min). |
| 3 | Tue Nov 24 only (Thanksgiving Break Nov 26-27 cuts Thursday's session) | Hold steady, short week | NMT warm-up. Bodyweight circuit only, no barbell this week - a short week isn't the place to add a new stimulus right before a 4-day break. No conditioning; let the week's natural rest do that job. |
| 4 | Tue Dec 1, Thu Dec 3 | Light barbell touches, all four lifts | NMT warm-up. Empty-bar/light-load technique work rotated across the two sessions: Tue - squat and bench (2-3x5, RPE 5-6); Thu - deadlift and overhead press (2-3x5, RPE 5-6). Still well short of anything that resembles a working set - the point is bar-path familiarity, not loading. Bodyweight accessory circuit stays in as a finisher. |
| 5 | Tue Dec 8, Thu Dec 10 | Testing Week lead-in | NMT warm-up only, then a brief movement screen on all four lifts - 1-2 sets each, RPE 4-5, split across the two sessions the same way Week 4 was. No conditioning, no volume. The goal this week is arriving at Dec 14 fresh and technically sharp, not adding one more training stimulus. |

Testing Week (Dec 14-18) opens as scheduled below, immediately after Week 5.

**Readiness rule for athletes who missed Pre-Testing Prep (added Oct 13, 2026 after an outside audit).** Pre-Testing Prep is attendance-optional, so being scheduled is not the same as being prepared. An athlete who attended neither Dec 8 nor Dec 10 (or most of the Prep block) does not test cold: on Testing Week's first day they run the NMT warm-up and the RPE 4-5 movement screen on all four lifts, and a lift's 5RM happens no earlier than their next Testing Week session and only after the coach has signed off clean technique on that lift. A lift without sign-off is tested at the Week 6 retest instead, with a coach-set conservative starting load until then.

**Four-workout re-entry rule (added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review).** The Research Report's transition-period standard (Safety: Transition Periods) calls for at least four separate non-maximal workouts before max-effort work after a break. Pre-Testing Prep is how athletes meet it. Count only Prep sessions the athlete actually attended and lifted in (from the attendance calendar or the coach's roll sheet). An athlete with **fewer than four** does not take a heavy 5RM in Testing Week, even with technique sign-off. Instead they work up to one top set of 5 capped at **RPE 7-8** (at least 2 clean reps left in reserve, no grinding, no missed-rep attempts), and that load - run through the same 5RM ÷ 0.87 conversion - is logged as a **provisional e1RM**, deliberately conservative. Their real 5RM happens at the **Week 6 retest or later**, by which point they've had Weeks 2-5 of programmed lifting. Anyone with four or more counted sessions tests normally.

**Returning from Winter Break.** Roughly 2.5 weeks separate Week 1's testing and the start of Week 2 (Dec 18 to Jan 4), most of which is the district's own closure, not a missed-training problem to solve - but it's still a real gap between establishing an e1RM and loading against it. Week 2 runs the same volume dip already built for Weeks 4/8 (3 work sets instead of 4, same prescribed %e1RM).

Opens with Testing Week (above), then 8 training weeks (Weeks 2-9).

Frequency: 4 days/week. During the school year, other sports are pulling kids and only 2 coaches are running this - 4 days keeps total weekly volume manageable without needing more coaching bandwidth than is actually available. Suggested days: Monday / Tuesday / Thursday / Friday, leaving Wednesday open for a school conflict make-up slot or pure NMT/mobility if someone needs it. **Athletes playing basketball or wrestling this phase** run the Multi-Sport Maintenance Track instead (see below) - a 2-day/week version at the same intensity.

**Session length: ~54 minutes** - ~7 min trimmed NMT warm-up (including the neck block), ~30 min main lift, ~15 min accessory circuit, ~2 min shoulder-health finisher (Day B and Day D carry the Nordic lower too - budget an extra 2-3 min on those two days, ~57 min total). These are firm targets, not ranges, so the room fits inside the window.

The single biggest risk to that window isn't the main lift, it's the accessory circuit's single-piece equipment (the one cable machine and one leg press). A pod of 4 taking turns on a single machine at ~60-90 sec/athlete costs that pod roughly 4-6 min per round at that station alone; across 3 rounds, a circuit built around one of those stations as its bottleneck can run closer to 20-25 min than the stated ~15, even with the flex-rotation rule below keeping different pods off each other's toes. **Default recommendation, not just a fallback:** for any pod larger than 2 at a single-piece station, use the dumbbell/band substitute from Equipment Substitutions as the day-one plan rather than waiting for the equipment to be occupied - it keeps the room inside the window instead of hoping the math works out live. **Recommended before the season starts:** run one full session with a stopwatch and confirm the pod-rotation math below actually clears in real time - the design should work on paper, but it hasn't been timed live yet, and the single-equipment stations are exactly where it's most likely to run long.

Structure for the room: with 10-15 kids and 3-4 racks, pods are capped at 3 athletes per rack for the main lift (see the worked math below for why). All pods lift the main lift simultaneously (no stagger, ~30 min timing model); each coach is assigned a fixed subset of racks to watch for the entire window rather than roaming: with 3-4 racks, Coach A takes racks 1-2 and Coach B takes racks 3-4 (with 3 racks, split 2/1 and alternate who takes the single rack week to week). A full pod's main-lift sequence is 8 sets (3 ramp + 4 work + 1 back-off - the set count doesn't change in Weeks 5/9, only the rep count within each work set drops, see Progression Scheme), run through the interleaved one-athlete-at-a-time turns described below with 2-3 min rest between work sets.

**The room-timing math, worked explicitly.** Modeling the interleaved rotation as continuous turn-taking - each athlete's rest between their own sets comes from watching pod-mates take theirs, not from a separately-added pause - against realistic per-set times (roughly 30-45 sec for a ramp set, 40-60 sec for a work set including the extra setup/spotting a heavier 75-85% e1RM load needs, 45-60 sec for the higher-rep back-off set) and the document's own 2-3 min rest requirement between work sets: a pod of 3 clears in roughly 17-23 minutes across that range of assumptions - comfortably inside the ~30 min window. A pod of 4 runs roughly 20-27 minutes under the same assumptions - tighter, and that range still doesn't include plate loading, bar transitions, or rack setup, none of which are free. That's the actual justification for capping at 3, not just a nice-to-have: it's the difference between a window that reliably clears and one that's betting on best-case turn times every session. Where the roster and rack count genuinely force a pod of 4 on a given day, don't assume it fits - confirm it live with a stopwatch first (see the recommendation above), and if it doesn't clear, trim volume rather than let the window run long into the accessory circuit.

**Coach supervision within a fixed 2-rack assignment.** A coach assigned 2 racks still can't watch two simultaneous live reps if both racks happen to have a lifter mid-rep at the same instant. The fix: offset the two racks' rotation start under one coach by roughly half a turn-cycle (e.g., Rack 1's pod starts its first ramp set immediately, Rack 2's pod waits about 20-30 seconds before starting theirs). With both racks cycling through turns at a similar pace but out of phase with each other, a coach's two racks essentially never both have a lifter mid-rep at once - there's a live rep on at most one of the coach's two racks at any given moment, so full visual attention can move between them without ever needing to split it. This costs nothing in total time (neither rack's own pace changes, only when it starts relative to the other) and it's a one-time verbal cue at the start of the block, not something that needs re-coordinating rep to rep. **This offset reduces simultaneous live reps; it does not guarantee that a coach is watching every rep (added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review).** Any set with external load that is ballistic or involves landing (the loaded jump-family work from Phase 2 on) needs a coach looking directly at that athlete for the whole set, which the offset can't promise. Run those sets sequentially with a coach watching, or keep the athlete on the unloaded version. Walk the actual room and rack layout before approving the rotation, and change the rack assignments where sight lines or distances don't work.

**The weight room's squat racks are equipped with safety pins/spotter arms.** This matters directly to the design above - the entire fixed-2-rack, phase-offset scheme is built to solve a coach's-eyes problem (making sure a live rep always has full visual attention), not a bare-catch problem. With mechanical pins or spotter arms set to each athlete's depth, a missed rep has a hard backstop even in the moment a coach's attention is on the other rack mid-offset-cycle - the room-timing and rotation math above is what keeps that moment rare, and the pins are what keeps it non-injurious if it happens anyway. Set pins/arms for every athlete before their first rep of the day, not just for anyone testing near a true max - the same standard as Testing Week.

Both coaches run the accessory circuit together once the main-lift block ends. Accessory work is a true circuit: each pod goes station 1, then 2, then 3, then 4 - one full lap - then repeats that same sequence two more times for a total of 3 rounds. It's not 3 rounds of station 1 before moving on. The 60-90 seconds is a per-athlete estimate (one person's set plus a short transition), not a per-pod clock - the room only has one cable machine and one leg press, so on equipment that only fits one athlete at a time, the pod takes turns: one athlete works while the others rest or spot, and that station takes roughly (pod size) x 60-90 sec to clear. Confirmed rule: pods move as a unit - nobody advances to the next station individually; the whole pod waits until the last athlete in that pod finishes their reps, then all move together. On equipment everyone can use at once - dumbbells, bodyweight movements like plank or lunges - the whole pod works simultaneously and that station clears in the same 60-90 sec. Because there's only one of several pieces of equipment shared across 3-4 pods, rotation isn't on a synchronized whistle - if a pod's next station is occupied by another pod, they flex to whichever open station comes next in their own sequence and circle back, rather than standing around waiting. Main lift sets at the rack work the same alternating way: pod members take turns one at a time through each set - ramp set 1, then the next athlete's ramp set 1, and so on around the pod, before anyone moves to their own next set. That's what keeps 3-4 athletes' worth of ramp, work, and back-off sets inside the ~30 min main-lift window instead of running each athlete through their whole sequence back to back; each athlete's rest is largely filled watching and spotting pod-mates' turns, and the coach at that rack should be checking bar path on every lifter's rep, not just whoever's currently up. Same logic applies to Testing Week.

**How an athlete is assigned to a lane.** The lane comes from the position(s) listed on the athlete's roster entry: OL/DL on both sides of the ball (or a single listed OL/DL position) is the lineman lane; any other recognised position, including LB and TE, is the skill lane. A two-way player with a lineman position on one side and a skill position on the other (OL/LB, DL/RB) alternates: skill lane on odd program weeks, lineman lane on even weeks. A blank or unrecognised position gets the standard prescription with no lane bias. These are coach-set conventions, not research findings.

Position-based load bias: same core lift and structure for everyone (full position-split isn't realistic with 2 coaches). Linemen run the main lift at the higher end of the prescribed load band (Progression Scheme below, including the 87%-of-e1RM ceiling in Weeks 5 and 9); reps stay the same for everyone at that week's prescribed count (5 most weeks, 4 in Weeks 5 and 9), so the bias is expressed through load, not rep count. Skill positions run the main lift at the lower end of the load range with the full prescribed reps. In the accessory circuit, core work stays for everyone - skill positions need it as much as anyone given the deceleration/cutting demands of the sport. Instead, skill positions swap out the day's more redundant lower-body accessory for the jump station described below, same body region but a power quality instead of a strength-endurance one: Day A swaps Calf Raise; Day B swaps Leg Press; Day C swaps Walking Lunge; Day D swaps Step-up. Circuit stays at 4 stations rather than growing to 5.

Every session opens with the NMT warm-up (~7 min trimmed in Phases 1, 2 and 5, FIFA 11+ style - strength, balance, light plyometric, and neck elements) before any lifting. This isn't optional and isn't just for game days; it's the standing injury-prevention layer under all five training phases, in-season included.

Nutrition & sleep: this phase's hypertrophy goal depends on both - adolescent athletes need roughly 1.2-2.0 g/kg/day of protein (above general adolescent guidelines) and 8-10 hours of sleep, and this age group commonly falls well short of both. Worth stating to the team - and probably parents - as an explicit part of the program, not an aside.

## Stop and Hand Off - Medical Interface (added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review)

This program has no medical protocol of its own and shouldn't invent one. Coaches don't diagnose, clear or treat anyone; these are the stop-and-hand-off lines, and they apply in every phase.

- **Suspected concussion:** remove the athlete from activity immediately, no same-day return, and hand off to the athletic trainer under Dover's concussion policy and the district's emergency action plan. The athlete doesn't resume lifting, sprinting, practice or games until the school's required medical clearance and graded return are complete, and the coach confirms that clearance with the athletic trainer before putting the athlete back into the program.
- **Illness, injury or a medical restriction:** follow the athletic-trainer and school process, and tie participation to the school's preparticipation exam. After a significant illness, injury or long interruption, bring the athlete back at an individually adjusted workload rather than dropping them into the current program week.
- **New or persistent pain** (joint, heel, knee, back or elsewhere), including pain that shows up during a growth spurt: stop or modify the exercise that provokes it, report it through the athletic trainer, and re-check technique and tolerance before restoring the prior load. Don't try to estimate maturity or growth-plate status from appearance.
- **Open item for the AD / athletic trainer:** who verifies and records medical clearance before an athlete rejoins, and how restrictions are passed to the coaches. Until that is named, the athletic trainer's word is the gate.

## NMT Warm-up Protocol

Runs before every session in **trimmed form (~6-7 min) in Phases 1, 2 and 5** and in full (~10 min) in Phases 3 and 4 (trim added Oct 21, 2026). Structured on the FIFA 11+ template referenced in the research report - three parts, running/activation into strength-balance-plyo into sport-specific movement. **Trimmed form for lift-only sessions: Part 2 every session, then 2 build-up sprints from Part 3; skip Part 1 and the rest of Part 3 (bounding, plant-and-cut).** Part 1 mostly raises body temperature and Part 3 rehearses field movements, and a barbell session already warms up under load through each lift's own ramp; Part 2 (core, neck, balance, landing) is the part a lift session doesn't otherwise train. The build-up sprints stay because they are the only sprint exposure these phases give athletes before Phase 3's testing window (see Phase 3, sprint runway): run them on a clear ~20-yard lane (field edge, gym floor, hallway), jog to stride to ~85-90% effort, never all-out. This is a coach decision to shorten the protocol, not something a trial tested - the NMT evidence in the Research Report is for multi-component programs, and the trimmed version keeps the strength, balance and landing components. Phases 3 and 4 (field speed, plyometric and conditioning days) keep all three parts. Same routine every session; the value is consistency and coaching quality, not variety. **The Nordic hamstring lower is not part of the pre-session warm-up in Phase 1: it runs post-session on Day B and Day D only (see Nordic Hamstring Lower - Dose and Frequency, below). The lateral bound (Part 2) runs post-session on Day A and Day B and stays in Part 2 on Day C and Day D, since neither of those days has a squat/hinge main lift.**

**Part 1 - Activation (3-4 min; Phases 3-4 only, skipped in the trimmed form):**

- Jog the width of the field/gym, easy pace
- High knees, one length
- Butt kicks, one length
- Carioca (both directions)
- Lateral shuffle (both directions)
- Backpedal, one length

**Part 2 - Strength, Balance, Plyo & Neck (5-6 min; every session in every phase), 2 sets each unless noted:**

- Plank hold with alternating shoulder taps - 20-30 sec
- Side plank (each side) - 20-30 sec
- **Neck 4-way isometric hold:** self-applied isometric hold - athlete presses their own flat hand against their own forehead (flexion), back of the head (extension), and each side of the head (lateral flexion) - 6-8 sec hold each direction, 1 set. Self-resistance removes the main risk of pairing 14-18-year-olds into uncoached partner resistance (turning it into an uneven push-off contest) while keeping the same isometric strength stimulus. **Where a coach can give hands-on 1:1 supervision to a specific pair** (not scalable to the full room with 2 coaches), partner-resisted manual holds are an acceptable substitute - coach or partner applies light, steady resistance with a flat hand, no jerking or sudden force. A rack-anchored 4-way neck harness/band, if the room has one, is another supervised-equivalent option. Adds roughly 60-90 seconds total either way. No forceful or ballistic neck loading, ever; neck pain, or a recent neck or head injury, means evaluation by the athletic trainer, not training through it.
- Single-leg balance reach (touch cone/ball in front, side, and back on one leg) - 6-8 reps/leg
- Bodyweight squat to calf/toe raise - 10 reps
- **Day A/Day B:** skip lateral bound here - it runs post-session instead (see below): a high-intensity plyometric right before a heavy squat/deadlift can subtly pre-fatigue the same core/hip stabilizers that lift needs. **Day C/Day D:** Lateral bound, stick the landing - 6-8 reps/side (neither day's main lift is a squat/hinge, so there's no equivalent conflict).

**Part 3 - Sport-Specific Movement (2-3 min; Phases 3-4 in full. Phases 1, 2 and 5 run only the build-up sprints):**

- Build-up sprints (jog to stride to near-top speed over ~20 yards) - 2-3 reps
- Bounding - one length
- Plant-and-cut (decelerate, cut 45-90 degrees, reaccelerate) - 3-4 reps each direction

## Nordic Hamstring Lower - Dose and Frequency (revised Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review)

**Frequency: 2 sessions a week in Phases 1 and 2** (Day B and Day D, post-session, right after the shoulder-health work) - never on consecutive days, never more than 3 in any 7 days. It previously ran on all four training days, well beyond the twice-weekly dose the Research Report cites, with adjacent-day exposures. Day B and Day D sit 3-4 days apart and neither is followed by a heavy squat or hinge within 24 hours.

**Dose: 2 sets per session** - partner holds ankles, controlled lowering toward the ground (regress to a slower, shorter-range version for anyone not ready for full range). Reps per set: weeks 1-3: 4-6; weeks 4-6: 6-8; weeks 7+: 8-10 (Phase 2 holds 8-10). A set ends when the athlete can no longer lower under control - that is the stopping rule, not a rep to push through. This is a coach-set, conservative schedule, not a validated adolescent-football dose: the Research Report found no Nordic injury-prevention trial in American football.

**Watch and back off:** more than mild next-day hamstring soreness, any hamstring pain or tightness while sprinting, or a visible drop in sprint speed means skip that session's Nordics and use 1 set next time; if it persists, send the athlete to the athletic trainer. Phase 3-4 and Phase 5 carry the same 2-set format on the days those documents name (Phase 5 maintenance: 2 sets x 6-8).

## Novice/Technique Onboarding Track

**Who actually uses this track.** This program's real incoming-freshman population - kids finishing 8th grade - doesn't reach this phase at all: they become eligible to join once their school year ends, which lands them in Phase 3's Testing Window (mid-to-late June), not here (mid-December). They're still in middle school when Phase 1 and Phase 2 run. So this track's actual users are narrower than "incoming freshmen": a true first-timer already enrolled at the high school who's starting the program mid-year for the first time (a non-football-playing underclassman picking up lifting, a late transfer, a walk-on), or any returning athlete flagged on the movement screen despite prior exposure. **The primary onboarding path for incoming freshmen is Phase 3's equivalent (see that document's Day D section)** - adapted to what Phase 3's Day D specifically requires (Bench/Pull-up/Overhead Press, not Squat/Hinge, since Phase 3 has no barbell lower-body lift).

**Duration and loading.** 3 weeks, RPE-based (RPE 6-7, meaning 3-4 reps in reserve) - not a percentage of anything, because there's no barbell max yet and shouldn't be one until movement quality is established. This isn't a hard 3-week cutoff: it's a floor, not a ceiling. An athlete who isn't clean and controlled across all four patterns at the end of Week 3 continues the track rather than being pushed into Testing Week's barbell tests on a calendar deadline - same technique-gated philosophy this program already uses elsewhere (Phase 2's Trap Bar Jump Squat prerequisite gate).

**Structure - same four patterns as the full program, dumbbell/goblet/bodyweight instead of barbell:**

- **Squat pattern:** Goblet Squat
- **Hinge pattern:** Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (bodyweight hip-hinge pattern first for anyone who needs it before adding even a light dumbbell)
- **Push pattern:** Dumbbell Bench Press, or push-up progression (incline against a bench, working toward full floor push-ups) for anyone not yet ready to control a dumbbell press
- **Pull pattern:** Inverted Row (barbell racked at hip height in a squat rack, same setup as this program's built-in pull-up substitute) or band-assisted row, working toward a true pull-up
- **Unilateral:** Bodyweight Split Squat, progressing toward a light-dumbbell Reverse Lunge by Week 3 - lays the groundwork for Day D's unilateral emphasis later

Same weekly frequency as whichever track this athlete will join after graduating (4 days if single-sport, 2 days if multi-sport), so the jump into the real template is a continuation, not a structural jolt. NMT warm-up runs in full, every session, unchanged - the injury-prevention case for it applies to a novice at least as much as anyone else in the room, arguably more.

**Progression across the 3 weeks:** Week 1: 3 sets x 8 reps, RPE 6 (comfortably submaximal - this week is about pattern quality, not effort). Week 2: 3 sets x 10 reps, RPE 6-7. Week 3: 3 sets x 10 reps, RPE 7 (some real effort, still 3+ reps in reserve) - by the end of this week, movement quality should be established enough to evaluate for graduation.

**Graduation checklist (coach sign-off, all four required before Testing Week's barbell tests):** full-depth squat under control, hips below knee crease, no heel rise or knee valgus collapse · neutral spine maintained through full hinge range of motion · full range-of-motion press without excessive lumbar arch to compensate · controlled pull with no kipping or momentum. An athlete who's clean on three of four but not the fourth keeps training all four patterns while getting extra coaching attention on the one that's lagging, rather than being held back entirely or pushed through on the other three's strength.

**Calendar note.** A flagged/novice athlete's actual Testing Week - and therefore their whole Progression Scheme calendar - starts up to 3 weeks later than the rest of the squad. That's fine: this doesn't need to be synced to when everyone else starts, even now that Phase 1 runs against fixed calendar dates (see Overview) - a delayed start for this small subgroup just means their own Week 1-9 numbering starts later on the calendar, not that the phase's own dates move. The movement screen itself still runs at what is now this track's start (not at the delayed Testing Week), so any single specific technique issue gets flagged and worked on from day one rather than three weeks in.

## Testing Week (Week 1)

Establishes each athlete's real working numbers so returning/experienced lifters aren't held to a beginner template and true beginners get gated by demonstrated technique, not assumed. This is a 5-rep max (5RM) test, not a true 1RM single - a safer technique check for this age group while still giving a real number to build from. **After testing, convert each recorded 5RM to an e1RM (5RM ÷ 0.87, nearest 2.5 lb) before Week 2 - that e1RM, not the raw 5RM, is what every load percentage in this program is calculated from.**

Testing ramp (applies to every 5RM test below, and to the Week 6 retest): there's no prior number to calculate percentages from on a testing day, so ramp conservatively - an empty-bar or bodyweight-only set, then 2-3 ascending sets building up gradually, resting 2-3 min between them, before attempting the top set of 5. Stop building and call that the 5RM once form starts to break down, even if it comes in under what the athlete expected - a clean lighter number is a better baseline than a shaky heavier one. This is also the moment to watch anyone flagged on the movement screen most closely, since load is actively increasing.

**Day 1 (Mon):**

- NMT warm-up
- Movement screen: coach watches each athlete through an unloaded squat and hinge pattern (bodyweight squat, RDL pattern with a dowel/empty bar). **Anyone flagged, and any true first-year novice regardless of screen result, starts the Novice/Technique Onboarding Track above instead of testing this week.**
- Back Squat: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM)

**Day 2 (Tue):** upper-body test day, deliberately placed between the two heavy lower-body tests

- NMT warm-up
- Bench Press: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM)
- Pull-up: the barbell ramp above doesn't apply here - warm up with 2 easy sets (3-5 reps each) instead, then attempt max strict bodyweight reps, no added weight, no assistance. Anyone hitting 8+ rests 5 min, then does a second test - work up to a weighted 5RM (added weight via belt or vest) - and **record the athlete's bodyweight (nearest pound) on the test day next to the added weight.** The Progression-table baseline for Day D is the **total system load - bodyweight plus added weight - not the added weight alone** (see "Weighted pull-up: percentages apply to total load" under the Progression Scheme). The rest matters: testing the weighted number immediately after a max-rep bodyweight set would understate it with residual fatigue. Anyone under 8 reps stops there; their baseline is that rep count, not a weight, and Day D progression for them is rep-based (see Day D). Anyone who can't do a bodyweight pull-up at all tests a lat pulldown or assisted pull-up 5RM instead, on the same rep-based track.

*Wednesday is a non-testing day.*

**Day 3 (Thu):**

- NMT warm-up
- Deadlift: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM) - about 72 hours after the squat test, so the deadlift baseline isn't taken on squat fatigue. Same stop-on-form-breakdown rule; record the heaviest clean set, and don't let the calendar or the athlete's expectations turn a clean lighter set into a failed near-max attempt.

**Day 4 (Fri):**

- NMT warm-up
- Overhead Press: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM)
- Make-ups: a missed bench or pull-up test is picked up here. A missed squat or deadlift is picked up here only if the other lower-body test was at least 48 hours earlier (or hasn't happened yet); otherwise it moves to the start of Week 2's first session, tested before that week's prescribed load - the same rule as OHP below.
- Record all numbers on a simple tracking sheet (name, lift, weight x 5) - convert each to e1RM before Week 2. This is what Weeks 2-9 load percentages are calculated from, and what gets compared at the next retest. Anyone who missed Friday's Overhead Press test picks it up at the start of Week 2's Day C session, testing before starting that week's prescribed load rather than skipping the baseline entirely.

## Weekly Template (Weeks 2-9)

Four days, each built around one primal movement pattern as the main lift, with an accessory circuit after. All main-lift loads are calculated from each athlete's Testing Week e1RM (see Progression, below, for the week-by-week percentages).

Missed a day: don't double up the next session to make it up - pick that lift back up at its next scheduled slot the following week.

**Next-day readiness rule (squat Monday, hinge Tuesday; added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review).** Before Day B's ramp, ask each athlete how the legs feel. Meaningful soreness or pain, or visibly degraded movement or bar speed during the ramp sets, means reduce the load and volume (the 3-set version, or Romanian Deadlift at a lighter load) or substitute an appropriate session. Never push the planned percentage to make up for reduced readiness. For an athlete who repeatedly doesn't recover, the coach can move that athlete's hinge day to Wednesday, the open slot.

### Day A — Squat (Monday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints; lateral bound omitted here, it runs post-session - see below)
- Main lift: Back Squat. Ramp: 50% x5, 65% x3, 75% x2 (off current e1RM, or the updated number after the Week 6 retest). Work: 4 sets x 5 reps at the week's prescribed % of e1RM (Progression table below) - in Week 2 that's 75%, so the last ramp set and the work sets land at the same percentage, which is intentional (ramp eases into work weight, it doesn't jump past it). **Two built-in exceptions to standard 4x5 (see Progression Scheme for the full reasoning behind each): Weeks 2, 4 and 8 trim to 3 sets instead of 4, same intensity - a scheduled volume dip (Week 2 for the return from Winter Break, Weeks 4 and 8 ahead of each block's peak); Weeks 5 and 9 trim to 4 reps instead of 5, same intensity - a peak-week rep-scheme fix.** Back-off: 1 set x 10-12 reps at a flat 65-70% of e1RM, controlled tempo (~2-3 sec lowering, brief pause, ~1-2 sec lifting - not explosive; max-intended bar speed is Phase 2's CAT work, kept out of Phase 1 on purpose so it lands as a genuinely new stimulus then). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station): Dumbbell Bench Press · Cable Row · Plank/Core (30-45 sec hold) · Calf Raise
- **Post-session finisher:** Shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2 sets x 15-20 reps), **then** Lateral bound, stick the landing - 6-8 reps/side (see NMT Warm-up Protocol above)

### Day B — Hinge (Tuesday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints; lateral bound omitted here, it runs post-session - see below)
- Main lift: Deadlift (alternate with Romanian Deadlift every other week to manage total spinal loading). On RDL weeks, the prescribed percentage is a ceiling, not a target - RDL mechanics and range of motion differ enough from a conventional deadlift that the same percentage of the tested e1RM often comes in lighter in practice; let the athlete's form set the actual weight, same as the auto-regulation rule below. Ramp: 50% x5, 65% x3, 75% x2 (off current e1RM, or the updated number after the Week 6 retest). Work: 4 sets x 5 reps at the week's prescribed % of e1RM. **Two built-in exceptions to standard 4x5 (see Progression Scheme for the full reasoning behind each): Weeks 2, 4 and 8 trim to 3 sets instead of 4, same intensity - a scheduled volume dip (Week 2 for the return from Winter Break, Weeks 4 and 8 ahead of each block's peak); Weeks 5 and 9 trim to 4 reps instead of 5, same intensity - a peak-week rep-scheme fix.** Back-off: 1 set x 10-12 reps at a flat 65-70% of e1RM, controlled tempo (~2-3 sec lowering, brief pause, ~1-2 sec lifting - not explosive; max-intended bar speed is Phase 2's CAT work, kept out of Phase 1 on purpose so it lands as a genuinely new stimulus then). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station): Overhead Press (dumbbell) · Pull-up or Band-Assisted Pull-up (bar-based, not the cable machine; 8-12 reps, stopping each set with roughly 2-3 clean reps still left before true failure - not the standard 12-15. Band tension is the adjustable variable here instead of weight: too easy (clearing 12 with way more than 3 left in the tank) means a lighter band; can't reach 8 even assisted means a heavier band) · Leg Press · Anti-rotation Core (Band Pallof Press, band anchored to a rack - not the cable machine, 10-12 reps per side)
- **Post-session finisher:** Shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2 sets x 15-20 reps), **then** Lateral bound, stick the landing - 6-8 reps/side, **then** Nordic hamstring lower (2 sets, see Nordic Hamstring Lower section)

### Day C — Push (Thursday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2, including the lateral bound, plus 2 build-up sprints; no Nordic on this day)
- Main lift: Bench Press. Ramp: 50% x5, 65% x3, 75% x2 (off current e1RM, or the updated number after the Week 6 retest). Work: 4 sets x 5 reps at the week's prescribed % of e1RM. **Two built-in exceptions to standard 4x5 (see Progression Scheme for the full reasoning behind each): Weeks 2, 4 and 8 trim to 3 sets instead of 4, same intensity - a scheduled volume dip (Week 2 for the return from Winter Break, Weeks 4 and 8 ahead of each block's peak); Weeks 5 and 9 trim to 4 reps instead of 5, same intensity - a peak-week rep-scheme fix.** Back-off: 1 set x 10-12 reps at a flat 65-70% of e1RM, controlled tempo (~2-3 sec lowering, brief pause, ~1-2 sec lifting - not explosive; max-intended bar speed is Phase 2's CAT work, kept out of Phase 1 on purpose so it lands as a genuinely new stimulus then). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station): Front Squat or Goblet Squat (lighter, technique-focused) · Dumbbell Row · Walking Lunge (10-12 reps per leg) · Hanging Knee Raise, 10-15 reps (Reverse Crunch on the floor if there's no bar free)
- Shoulder-health finisher (2 sets x 15-20 reps), right after the accessory circuit

### Day D — Pull / Unilateral (Friday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2, including the lateral bound, plus 2 build-up sprints; Nordic runs post-session, see below)
- Main lift: pick the track based on Testing Week's bodyweight max-rep pull-up test.
  - **Weighted Pull-up track** (8+ bodyweight reps at testing): ramp with 2 sets of bodyweight reps (5 reps, then 3 reps) to prime the pattern, then work sets - 4 sets x 5 reps at the week's prescribed % of the **total-system-load** e1RM (bodyweight + added weight, Progression table below), then subtract bodyweight to get the belt/vest load - see "Weighted pull-up: percentages apply to total load" under the Progression Scheme - **two built-in exceptions, same as the other main lifts: Weeks 2, 4 and 8 trim to 3 sets instead of 4 (scheduled volume dip); Weeks 5 and 9 trim to 4 reps instead of 5 (peak-week rep-scheme fix) - see Progression Scheme** - then a back-off set of 10-12 bodyweight-only reps (no added weight) in place of the usual back-off, since bodyweight already sits well under the working load - same controlled tempo as the other back-off sets (~2-3 sec lowering, brief pause, ~1-2 sec lifting, not explosive). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
  - **Bodyweight/Assisted Pull-up track** (under 8 reps at testing, or Row if pull-ups aren't yet clean under any assistance level): 2 warm-up sets of 3-5 easy reps, then 4 sets x max reps (3 sets in Weeks 2, 4 and 8, the scheduled volume-dip weeks), working toward 8+ to graduate onto the Weighted track mid-phase; no back-off set needed since these sets are already sub-maximal volume, not a heavy top end.
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds unless noted, 12-15 reps/station): Overhead Press (barbell) - this is where Friday's OHP test actually gets used: 3 sets x 5 reps (3 x 4 in Weeks 5 and 9, the same peak-week rep-scheme fix as the main lifts) at the week's prescribed % of the tested OHP e1RM (Progression table below), not found weight, resting 90 sec-2 min between sets since the load runs meaningfully heavier than a typical accessory. No position-based bias band here (that's reserved for the four main lifts) - same prescribed % for everyone. Remaining stations: · Single-leg Romanian Deadlift (10-12 reps per leg) · Step-up (10-12 reps per leg) · Cable Woodchopper, 10-12 reps per side
- **Post-session finisher:** Shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2 sets x 15-20 reps) **then** Nordic hamstring lower (2 sets, see Nordic Hamstring Lower section)

**Accessory weight selection:** 12-15 reps is a standard hypertrophy-dosing rep range - it's why the accessory circuit is built at higher reps than the main lift's 5s. These stations don't have a Testing Week baseline like the main lifts, though, so use the "found weight" method - athlete picks a weight where the last 1-2 reps of the last set are genuinely hard but form holds (roughly 2-3 reps in reserve). Write that weight down; once all 3 rounds at 12-15 reps feel clearly easy on the last set, add weight the following week. (Exceptions: Day B's Pull-up station uses its own 8-12 rep range and band tension instead of weight; Day D's Overhead Press station uses the tested OHP e1RM and the weekly Progression percentage instead of found weight - see each day's entry.) Coach spot-checks form on the first round each session, especially early weeks.

**Shoulder-health finisher (every session):** Face pull or band pull-apart, 2 sets x 15-20 reps, light band or low cable pulley. On Day C, it runs right after the accessory circuit. On Day A it runs first, followed by the lateral bound; on Day B, followed by the lateral bound and then the Nordic hamstring lower; on Day D, followed directly by the Nordic hamstring lower (see Post-Session Finisher above). **Day A and Day B specifically:** the lateral bound also relocates here, between the shoulder-health work and (on Day B) the Nordic lower; Day C and Day D keep it in the pre-session warm-up since neither day's main lift is a squat/hinge. Phase 1 has real pressing volume spread across all four days, not just one heavy bench day: Bench Press is Day C's main lift, Overhead Press is an accessory station on both Day B (dumbbell) and Day D (barbell, at the tested % of e1RM - the heaviest accessory load in the program), and Dumbbell Bench Press is Day A's accessory. Light scapular/rotator-cuff stabilizer work under that much pressing volume is standard practice. Unlike the Nordic hamstring lower, this doesn't need to progress in volume - the point is consistent light-load stabilizer work, not a strength stimulus, so it stays at 2x15-20 all phase.

**Skill-position plyo swap:** skill positions use this jump station in place of that day's redundant lower-body accessory (per Overview, above) - Calf Raise on Day A, Leg Press on Day B, Walking Lunge on Day C, Step-up on Day D. Core work (Plank, Pallof Press, Hanging Knee Raise, Cable Woodchopper) stays in the circuit for everyone, every day. Pick one for the week and keep it consistent. **Box Jump:** box height 12-18 inches to start (low enough to land on top under control - only raise it once an athlete lands quiet and stable, not once they can technically clear it); athlete stands close to the box, swings arms, jumps explosively up onto the box landing softly with both feet flat, then steps down one foot at a time (never jumps down) - 3 sets x 5 reps, full reset between reps. **Hop Series** (2 rounds): Lateral Hop over a cone x 8 reps (side to side, sticking the landing before the next hop), Forward-Back Hop over a cone x 8 reps (same, front to back), Single-Leg Hop for distance x 5 reps per leg - hop forward on one leg as far as a controlled landing allows, stick it fully (no double-hop) before resetting for the next rep; this is a forward distance hop with a stuck landing each time, not continuous bounding and not a hop in place.

## Multi-Sport Maintenance Track

Basketball and wrestling both run through the heart of this phase's window (mid-December through late February), and any athlete playing one of them can't reliably make 4 lifting days a week on top of their other sport's practice and game schedule. This track is the answer: same intensity as the full 4-day track, compressed into 2 days a week, with accessory volume cut rather than main-lift intensity.

**Who uses it.** Any athlete whose other-sport commitments conflict with 2 or more of the 4 weekly slots. Coach judgment, not a rigid rule - an athlete whose conflicts ease up mid-phase (their other sport's season ends, a schedule opens up) can move onto the full 4-day track from that point forward, and the reverse. It's a track to move between, not a permanent assignment.

**What stays, what's cut:**

- NMT warm-up (trimmed form - Part 2 including the neck block, plus 2 build-up sprints): every session, no exceptions - if anything, a two-sport athlete's total injury exposure across two activities makes this layer more important, not less, and it's the cheapest, lowest-fatigue-cost part of the program to keep in full.
- Nordic hamstring lower: 2 sets post-session on Track Day 2 (the hinge day) always, and on Track Day 1 too only if the two track days are at least 48 hours apart; never on consecutive days. Same dose and rep progression as the full track (Nordic Hamstring Lower section).
- Lateral bound: both Track Day 1 (squat) and Track Day 2 (hinge) move it out of the pre-session warm-up to post-session, since both days carry a squat or hinge main lift.
- Shoulder-health finisher: unchanged, both days.
- Main lift ramp and work sets: same % of e1RM as the full track's Progression Scheme table for that week - intensity isn't reduced. Work sets trim from 4 to 3 (still enough to train the pattern at the prescribed load without the extra volume a 4-day athlete gets).
- Back-off set: kept, unchanged (65-70% e1RM, 10-12 reps) - low time cost, meaningful hypertrophy/technique value.
- Accessory circuit: cut entirely on this track. This is the actual time savings - roughly 15 minutes per session that would otherwise go to accessory work the athlete's other sport is substantially covering already.
- Overhead Press: not a percentage-based main lift on this track (there's no time budget for a third full lift per day without undoing the time savings the track exists for). Still tested at Testing Week and the Week 6 retest if the athlete can make that session, so the e1RM number exists for Phase 4/5 reference later - see Testing Week note below. That number is a rougher, less-maintained baseline than the Squat/Bench/Deadlift/Pull-up numbers this track trains weekly - treat it as a starting estimate for Phase 2, not a tightly tracked number. Track Day 1's post-session finisher includes 2 sets x 10-12 reps of light dumbbell Overhead Press, found-weight and well submaximal (see below) - a maintenance touch to keep the pattern and overhead shoulder ROM trained, not a loading stimulus meant to build the lift.

**Technique re-familiarization before the Week 6 barbell retest.** The dumbbell maintenance touch above keeps the shoulder trained, but it doesn't keep the barbell pattern grooved - by Week 6, this athlete hasn't gripped a bar overhead in six weeks, and going straight into a cold 5RM test risks shoulder impingement from an unpracticed lift under near-maximal load. Track Day 1's session in the week immediately before Week 6 (and again before any later retest) replaces the light dumbbell OHP touch with 2 sets x 5 reps of barbell Overhead Press at a found, clearly submaximal weight (RPE 5-6, empty bar or close to it if needed) - a technique re-acquaintance rep under the actual bar, not a loading stimulus, so the retest itself is the second barbell OHP touch that week, not the first.

**Track Day 1 — Squat + Push:**

- NMT warm-up (trimmed form: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints)
- Back Squat: ramp (50%x5, 65%x3, 75%x2 off e1RM), then 3 sets x 5 reps at the week's prescribed % of e1RM (Progression Scheme table below - **Weeks 5 and 9 drop to 3 sets x 4 reps at 85% e1RM, same reasoning as the full track**), then back-off (1x10-12 @ 65-70% e1RM)
- Bench Press: same ramp/work/back-off structure, at Bench e1RM
- Post-session finisher: shoulder-health work (2x15-20), **then 2 sets x 10-12 reps light dumbbell Overhead Press, found-weight and submaximal (a maintenance touch for overhead pressing capacity, not a loading stimulus - see Overhead Press note above)**, **then Lateral bound, stick the landing - 6-8 reps/side (see What Stays, What's Cut above)**, then Nordic hamstring lower only if the two track days are 48+ hours apart

**Track Day 2 — Hinge + Pull:**

- NMT warm-up (trimmed form: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints)
- Deadlift (alternate with Romanian Deadlift every other week, same rule as the full track): same ramp/work/back-off structure, at Deadlift e1RM
- Pull-up: same track logic as the full program's Day D (Weighted or Bodyweight/Assisted, based on Testing Week) - work sets at the week's prescribed % of e1RM (weighted track) or max reps (bodyweight track), trimmed to 3 sets like the main lifts
- Post-session finisher: shoulder-health work (2x15-20), **then Lateral bound, stick the landing - 6-8 reps/side (see What Stays, What's Cut above)**, then Nordic hamstring lower

**Session length:** roughly 40-45 minutes per day (~7 min NMT, ~13-15 min per main lift, ~2-4 min finisher, Track Day 1 running 2-3 min longer than Day 2 for the added light Overhead Press touch) - shorter than the full track's ~57-60 min sessions despite covering two lift patterns, since there's no accessory circuit to run.

**Testing Week note:** the same 4-day Testing Week structure applies, but a two-sport athlete may only be able to make 2 of those days. Prioritize the four lifts this track trains weekly (squat, bench, deadlift, pull-up) over Overhead Press based on scheduling, and keep the squat and deadlift tests at least 48 hours apart; missed tests (including Overhead Press, which isn't part of the weekly rotation but still needs a baseline) get picked up at the Week 6 retest or the next available session, same allowance the full track already uses for a missed Friday OHP test.

## Progression Scheme

Main lift loads are set as a percentage of each athlete's Testing Week **e1RM**, and increase weekly. This is a standard linear progression, appropriate for a group with mixed training age:

Position-based load bias, applied on top of the table below: linemen run at the upper end of a band of +/-2.5 percentage points around the prescribed percentage (e.g., 80% becomes up to 82.5%) with reps held at that week's prescribed count (max-strength lane). **Peak-week cap: in Weeks 5 and 9 the lineman ceiling is 87% of e1RM, not 87.5%.** Because e1RM = 5RM ÷ 0.87, 87% of e1RM is exactly the athlete's tested 5RM load, and 4x4 repeated at a load above what they showed for a single set of five isn't supported by the test. Treat 87% as a ceiling, not a target: the existing autoregulation rule still applies, and a set that grinds or slows noticeably means the next set drops back toward the prescribed percentage. The bias applies as written in every other week.; skill positions run at the lower end of that band, same rep count, with the swapped-in Jump Station noted above.

**Weighted pull-up: percentages apply to total load (added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review).** On the Weighted Pull-up track, the resistance the athlete moves is bodyweight plus whatever is on the belt or vest, so the % of e1RM is taken on that **total system load**, not on the added weight alone. Method: (1) at the test, record bodyweight (BW) and the added weight of the 5RM; (2) total 5RM load = BW + added; (3) e1RM(total) = total 5RM load ÷ 0.87; (4) each week's prescribed total = prescribed % x e1RM(total); (5) **belt/vest load = prescribed total - current BW**, rounded to the nearest 2.5 lb. If that number is zero or negative, the athlete does the work sets at bodyweight - never negative, never assisted on this track. Re-weigh the athlete at each retest and at Week 5. Worked example: BW 170, 5RM added 25 -> total 195 -> e1RM(total) 224.1; Week 2 at 75% = 168 -> bodyweight only; Week 9 at 85% = 190.5 -> +20 lb. (Calculating off the added weight alone would have put Week 2 at roughly 98% of the athlete's tested total load.) The same convention applies in every later phase that carries the weighted pull-up baseline forward.

**Scheduled volume dip (Weeks 4 and 8).** Weeks 4 and 8 - the week immediately before each block's Week 5/Week 9 peak - trim from 4 work sets to 3, at the same prescribed intensity (see Progression Scheme table and each day's entry). It's a volume dip, not an intensity reduction, so it doesn't undercut the linear-progression logic driving the rest of the block - it's scheduled and unconditional, happening whether or not any athlete has missed a rep. Week 6's retest, auto-regulation, and Phase 4's taper remain the program's other fatigue-management points. **Not extended to the Multi-Sport Maintenance Track:** that track already runs at reduced volume (3 work sets, not 4, every week) and its athletes get additional load variability from their other sport that single-sport athletes don't have - stacking a further volume cut onto an already-reduced track risks under-dosing it rather than protecting it.

Auto-regulation: if an athlete can't complete all reps at the prescribed load on a given day (missed sleep, other-sport fatigue, etc.), drop the load 5-10% for that session rather than grinding out failed reps - consistent with the "technique and consistency over one bad day's number" principle running through this whole program. Log it, don't chase it.

**Weeks 5 and 9** run 4 sets x 4 reps (3 sets x 4 reps on the Multi-Sport Track) at 85% of e1RM, instead of 4x5. Auto-regulation (drop 5-10% if the prescribed reps aren't there) still applies as described above.

| Week | Main Lift Load (% of e1RM) | Back-off Set | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 75% | 65-70% of e1RM, 10-12 reps | **3x5, not 4x5** - post-Winter-Break return, same volume dip as Weeks 4 and 8; reintroduction and technique check under load |
| 3 | 80% | 65-70% of e1RM, 10-12 reps | |
| 4 | 82.5% | 65-70% of e1RM, 10-12 reps | **3x5, not 4x5** - scheduled volume dip before Week 5's peak, see note above |
| 5 | 85% | 65-70% of e1RM, 10-12 reps | **4x4, not 4x5** (Multi-Sport Track: 3x4) - see note above |
| 6 | Retest week — re-establish 5RM on all five tested lifts - squat, bench, deadlift, pull-up, and OHP (same structure as Testing Week - Mon squat, Tue bench + pull-up, Thu deadlift, Fri OHP + make-ups); convert each new 5RM to e1RM | — | Confirms progress, resets the e1RM base for weeks 7-9 |
| 7 | 78% of new e1RM | 65-70% of new e1RM, 10-12 reps | Slightly conservative restart post-retest |
| 8 | 82% of new e1RM | 65-70% of new e1RM, 10-12 reps | **3x5, not 4x5** - scheduled volume dip before Week 9's peak, see note above |
| 9 | 85% of new e1RM | 65-70% of new e1RM, 10-12 reps | **4x4, not 4x5** (Multi-Sport Track: 3x4) - see note above. Closes Phase 1; these e1RM numbers carry into Phase 2's testing week as the new baseline |

## Equipment Substitutions

For when a station's primary equipment is occupied by another pod, broken, or otherwise unavailable.

| Exercise | Primary Equipment | Substitute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Back Squat | Barbell + rack | Goblet Squat or Front Squat, dumbbells racked at the shoulders |
| Deadlift | Barbell | Trap Bar Deadlift, or Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift if no bar at all |
| Romanian Deadlift | Barbell | Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift |
| Bench Press | Barbell + bench | Dumbbell Bench Press |
| Overhead Press (barbell) | Barbell | Dumbbell Overhead Press - since this station is normally tied to a tested OHP e1RM, treat this one session as found-weight instead (pick a weight for 3x5 with 2-3 reps in reserve) rather than trying to convert the percentage |
| Pull-up / Weighted Pull-up | Pull-up bar | Band-Assisted Pull-up (already the built-in second track) if the bar's occupied but full reps still fit the moment; for added weight with no belt/vest available, hold a dumbbell between the feet or wear a loaded backpack. If the pull-up bar area itself is unavailable: Inverted Row, using a barbell racked at hip height in a squat rack - body underneath, chest to bar - same pulling pattern, different setup |
| Dumbbell Bench Press (accessory) | Dumbbells | Push-ups, same rep count |
| Cable Row | Cable machine | Dumbbell Row or Band Row |
| Calf Raise | Dumbbells (optional) | Bodyweight Calf Raise, paused at the top |
| Overhead Press, dumbbell (accessory) | Dumbbells | Band Overhead Press |
| Leg Press | Leg press machine | Goblet Squat or Walking Lunge |
| Band Pallof Press | Resistance band + anchor | Suitcase Carry (one dumbbell, walk a set distance each side) - not identical, but hits the same anti-rotation demand |
| Front Squat / Goblet Squat | Barbell or dumbbell | Bodyweight Squat, paused at the bottom |
| Dumbbell Row | Dumbbells | Cable Row (if the machine's free) or Band Row |
| Hanging Knee Raise | Pull-up bar | Reverse Crunch on the floor (already the built-in alternative) |
| Single-leg Romanian Deadlift | Dumbbell (optional) | Bodyweight single-leg RDL |
| Step-up | Plyo box or bench | Bottom bleacher step, or any stable platform roughly 12-18 inches |
| Cable Woodchopper | Cable machine | Band Woodchopper, band anchored to a rack |
| Box Jump | Plyo box | Hop Series (already the built-in second option for the skill-position jump station) |
| Cones (warm-up touches, Hop Series markers) | Cones | Any small marker - water bottle, shoe, folded towel |

# Phase 2 — Spring Program (Strength-Speed & Power)

*September 20, 2026 · Kenneth Quinones, Assistant Football Coach LB/RB, Dover High School*

## Overview

Dates, anchored to Dover Public Schools' confirmed 2026-2027 district calendar and to Phase 1's own anchored end date: Testing Week (Week 1) runs **Monday, March 1 - Friday, March 5, 2027**, starting immediately after Phase 1's Week 9 ends (Feb 26) - consistent with this document's own existing position that Phase 2 starts right where Phase 1 ends, no layoff. Weeks 2-11 (10 training weeks) then run as follows:

| Week | Dates | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Week 2 | Mar 8-12, 2027 | — |
| Week 3 | Mar 15-19, 2027 | — |
| Week 4 | Mar 22-26, 2027 | Friday Mar 26 is the district's first Spring Break closure day - that week's Day D session is missed. Per the standard missed-day rule this gets picked up "at the next scheduled slot," but the next scheduled slot here is on the far side of Spring Break - so it's simply absorbed into the break rather than made up, the same way a missed day immediately before a longer closure is handled elsewhere in this program. **Thursday Mar 25 (Day C) is also flagged:** it's one of the district calendar's five contingent "emergency day" dates - closed by default, and only opens as an actual school day if the year ends up using at least 2 of its budgeted emergency (snow) days elsewhere. Plan Day C as written; if it turns out closed, the standard missed-day rule applies the same as any other closure. |
| Spring Break | Mar 26 - Apr 2, 2027 (closure starts Friday, Mar 26) | No formal training. School resumes Monday, April 5. |
| Week 5 | Apr 5-9, 2027 | First week back - see the transition-period note below. **Friday Apr 9 is a staff in-service, single-session day for students:** Day D still runs, but the coach sets the time (after school or a shortened session). |
| Week 6 | Apr 12-16, 2027 | — |
| Week 7 | Apr 19-23, 2027 | Retest week. |
| Week 8 | Apr 26-30, 2027 | — |
| Week 9 | May 3-7, 2027 | — |
| Week 10 | May 10-14, 2027 | — |
| Week 11 | May 17-21, 2027 | Closes Phase 2. **Monday May 17 (Day A) is flagged:** also one of the district calendar's five contingent "emergency day" dates, closed by default and opening as an actual school day once the year has used at least 1 of its 5 budgeted emergency (snow) days elsewhere - the easiest of the five to trip into becoming a real school day, and the one most likely to actually run in a typical year. Plan Day A as written; the missed-day rule covers it if it's closed. |

Phase 2 runs early March through late May. Memorial Day (Mon, May 31, 2027) falls after Phase 2's Week 11 ends, so it doesn't intersect the 11 training weeks; it does fall inside the Phase 2–3 Bridge (see below).

**Week 11's close is no longer the last structured session before Phase 3.** See the Phase 2–3 Bridge section (after Equipment Substitutions, below) for what actually runs between this phase's close and Phase 3's Testing Window.

**Returning from Spring Break.** Unlike Phase 1's Week 2, this isn't a return from Testing Week - it lands mid-progression, where the original Week 5 prescription was 84% e1RM x4 (Strength Lane; revised below to 78% x3) and 65% Bench e1RM (Power Lane), climbing toward Week 6's peak before the Week 7 retest. Resuming at that intensity cold, after an 8-day closure, is a different situation than a normal mid-phase week (Phase 1-to-Phase 2 has no layoff; this does). **Week 5's Strength Lane runs 78% e1RM x3 reps, not 84% x4.** The volume cut stays (3 reps, not 4) alongside the intensity cut - both move together for this one week, not one or the other. The Power Lane stays at its prescribed 65% as written; CAT work is already submaximal by design (50-70% range, moved for speed rather than ground out), so it doesn't carry the same fatigue-accumulation risk the Strength Lane's climbing percentage does.

There's no separate transition-period week for the Phase 1-to-Phase 2 boundary itself; the adjustment above is specific to Spring Break landing mid-phase.

Opens with Testing Week (above), then 10 training weeks (Weeks 2-11).

Frequency: 4 days/week, same as Phase 1 and for the same reasons - still school year, still 2 coaches, still other sports pulling kids, still roughly 10-15 athletes. Suggested days: Monday / Tuesday / Thursday / Friday, Wednesday open for make-up or mobility. **Spring-sport athletes** (track, baseball, softball, lacrosse, tennis, and others - this phase's window covers essentially the whole spring season) run the Multi-Sport Maintenance Track instead (see below).

Structure for the room: same pod system as Phase 1 - pods **capped at 3 athletes per rack** (firm default), alternating turns through both lanes the same way Phase 1's pods alternated through ramp and work sets. **Room supervision:** all pods run the Strength Lane simultaneously, with each coach assigned a fixed subset of racks to watch for the full window (e.g., Coach A racks 1-2, Coach B racks 3-4) instead of roaming all of them alone. A coach assigned 2 racks offsets the two racks' rotation start by roughly half a turn-cycle, so a coach's two racks essentially never both have a live rep at the same instant - full attention can move between them without splitting it, at no cost to total time. **That is an attention aid, not a guarantee of continuous supervision (see Phase 1):** the loaded Trap Bar Jump Squat and Jump Shrug need a coach looking directly at that athlete for the whole set, so run jump sets one athlete at a time with a coach watching, or keep the athlete on the unloaded version, and check the real room layout before approving the rack assignments. On Day C, Strength Lane and Power Lane use the same bench (just a lighter bar moved faster), so there's no travel between them. On Days A, B, and D, the Power Lane exercise needs different equipment than the Strength Lane one - a trap bar instead of the squat bar on Day A, a trap bar instead of the deadlift bar on Day B, a landmine or medicine ball instead of the pull-up bar on Day D - so the whole pod moves together to that equipment once everyone's finished the Strength Lane, the same "pod moves as a unit" rule from Phase 1. If trap bars or landmine stations are fewer in number than racks, pods flex to whichever's open rather than waiting in lockstep - the same rule Phase 1 used for its one cable machine. Neither jump-family Power Lane movement (Trap Bar Jump Squat, Trap Bar Jump Shrug) needs any more coaching attention than a normal pod rotation gets - no technique-gating apparatus, no coach-split rule; that supervision demand left the program along with Hang Clean. Accessory circuit runs the same true-circuit rotation (station by station, repeat for 3 rounds) described in the Phase 1 document; that mechanic doesn't change here. **The room's squat racks carry safety pins/spotter arms**, which is the mechanical backstop the fixed-rack, phase-offset design above assumes - it's what keeps a rare missed-attention moment non-injurious, not a reason to change the rotation itself.

**How an athlete is assigned to a lane.** The lane comes from the position(s) listed on the athlete's roster entry: OL/DL on both sides of the ball (or a single listed OL/DL position) is the lineman lane; any other recognised position, including LB and TE, is the skill lane. A two-way player with a lineman position on one side and a skill position on the other (OL/LB, DL/RB) alternates: skill lane on odd program weeks, lineman lane on even weeks. A blank or unrecognised position gets the standard prescription with no lane bias. These are coach-set conventions, not research findings.

Position-based load and velocity bias: same core lift and structure for everyone. Linemen run the Strength Lane at the higher end of the prescribed load band (as in Phase 1) and the Power Lane at the heavier end of its percentage range with a coaching emphasis on controlled, powerful bar speed rather than maximal velocity. Skill positions run the Strength Lane at the lower end of the load band and the Power Lane at the lighter end of its percentage range with a coaching emphasis on maximal intended bar speed. Same lift, same sets and reps for everyone - the bias is expressed through load and velocity coaching cues, not different exercises.

NMT warm-up: the same trimmed form as Phase 1 (Part 2, including the self-resisted neck block, plus 2 build-up sprints; Part 1 and the rest of Part 3 are dropped for lift sessions), except there is no lateral bound here (the jump-family work already lives in the Power Lane). **Nordic hamstring lower: 2 sets on Day B and Day D, post-session only** (never consecutive days; reps at Phase 1's weeks-7+ dose, 8-10 per set; same back-off rules for soreness or hamstring symptoms) - see the Phase 1 document, "Nordic Hamstring Lower - Dose and Frequency." **Also carried over from Phase 1:** the stop-and-hand-off rules (concussion, injury or illness, new or persistent pain) and the next-day readiness rule for the squat-Monday, hinge-Tuesday pairing apply unchanged. Not repeated in full here.

Nutrition & sleep: same standing requirement as Phase 1 (1.2-2.0 g/kg/day protein, 8-10 hours of sleep) - still applies, still worth restating to the team as training demands escalate heading toward summer conditioning and camp.

## Testing Week (Week 1)

Re-establishes each athlete's working numbers using the same 5RM protocol as Phase 1 (not a true 1RM), plus one new addition: a power marker, since this phase is built around power expression and Phase 1 never measured it. **As in Phase 1, convert every tested 5RM to e1RM (÷ 0.87) immediately after testing - that e1RM is what every percentage in this phase's Progression Scheme is calculated from.**

Testing ramp: similar spirit to Phase 1's rule, adapted for a real difference - Phase 1's ramp existed because there was no prior number at all. Here there is one (Phase 1's Week 9 e1RM), so ramp off that: 2-3 ascending sets building toward it, resting 2-3 min between them, before the top set of 5. Same stop-on-form-breakdown rule applies - a clean number under expectations still beats a shaky one at it. Same ramp rule applies at the Week 7 retest too, just ramping off Week 6's e1RM instead of Phase 1's.

**Day 1 (Mon):**

- NMT warm-up
- Vertical Jump (new): do this first, right after NMT and before any heavy lifting (Monday, so it's taken fresh and ahead of both lower-body tests) - 3 attempts, best recorded. Standing reach mark first (chalk on fingertips, mark the wall at full reach), then max-effort jump touch, chalking the highest point reached - the gap between the two marks is the score. A jump mat or Vertec works the same way if the room has one, but the wall-and-chalk version needs nothing beyond what's already in the room. This is the phase's power baseline - testing it before the squat, deadlift and pull-up matters, since fatigue from a heavy lift or a max-rep pull-up set would understate true power output.
- Back Squat: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM)

**Day 2 (Tue):** upper-body test day, deliberately placed between the two heavy lower-body tests

- NMT warm-up
- Bench Press: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM)
- Pull-up: same bodyweight-then-weighted protocol as Phase 1's Testing Week (including recording bodyweight on test day, since the weighted baseline is total system load, not added weight alone) - re-test from scratch, since athletes can graduate from the Bodyweight/Assisted track to the Weighted track between phases

*Wednesday is a non-testing day.*

**Day 3 (Thu):**

- NMT warm-up
- Deadlift: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM) - about 72 hours after the squat test, so the deadlift baseline isn't taken on squat fatigue. Same stop-on-form-breakdown rule; record the heaviest clean set.

**Day 4 (Fri):**

- NMT warm-up
- Overhead Press: work up to a heavy set of 5 (5RM)
- Make-ups: a missed bench or pull-up test is picked up here. A missed squat or deadlift is picked up here only if the other lower-body test was at least 48 hours earlier (or hasn't happened yet); otherwise it moves to the start of Week 2's first session, tested before that week's prescribed load.
- Record all numbers (squat, bench, deadlift, overhead press, pull-up track, vertical jump) on the tracking sheet, converting each 5RM to e1RM - this is what Weeks 2-11 percentages are calculated from, and what the Week 7 retest compares against.

**Prerequisite gate for loaded jump-family work (applies to Day A's Trap Bar Jump Squat, Day B's Trap Bar Jump Shrug, and the Multi-Sport Track's equivalents, all phase; reworked Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review so it applies to every athlete, linemen included).** This is a behavioral, coach-observable standard, not a medical screen. **Every athlete - skill or lineman, returning or first-year - takes a coach-observed, unloaded landing assessment in Testing Week (Day 1 or Day 4, or the first Week 2 session for anyone who misses it) before any external load goes on a jump.** The coach watches 3 box-jump-and-stick landings (low box, 12-18 inches, bodyweight) and 3 forward broad-jump landings, and records **pass or defer** on the tracking sheet. Pass = quiet, two-footed landing, knees tracking over the toes without caving in, hips back, and the landing held for about 2 seconds with no extra steps. Phase 1's jump-station work (skill positions only) is useful history but is not a substitute: linemen didn't do it, and "struggled with landing" was a judgment nobody was required to record. An athlete who defers - or who is any true first-year novice - runs the Power Lane as an unloaded Countermovement Jump or Medicine Ball Scoop Toss instead: same 5 sets x 3 reps, same maximal-intent cue, no load. Re-assess a deferred athlete every 2 weeks and move them up once they pass; also re-check anyone whose landing visibly changes or who reports new pain (see Stop and Hand Off in the Phase 1 document). The criteria above are coach-set conventions, not a validated test. This is the same Power Lane slot with the load swapped out, at the coach's judgment - not a separate track to build or maintain.

## Weekly Template (Weeks 2-11)

Same four-day pattern as Phase 1 - each day anchored around one primal movement for its Strength Lane - but each day now runs a Strength Lane and a Power Lane back to back instead of a single main lift. A couple of Power Lane movements extend past that single pattern on purpose: Day B's Trap Bar Jump Shrug is closer to a full-body pull-and-extend than a pure hinge, and Day D's rotational work isn't one of the six primal patterns at all - it's its own football-specific quality. No back-off set this phase; the Power Lane fills that role. Missed a day: same rule as Phase 1 - don't double up, pick it back up at the next scheduled slot.

One structural note: Phase 1's skill-position jump-station swap in the accessory circuit is retired this phase. It existed there because nothing else in that phase gave skill positions a speed-specific stimulus. Phase 2's Power Lane already does that job for everyone, expressed through the velocity coaching cue described in the Overview - so the accessory circuit runs the same for every position this phase, no swap needed.

Another note worth being explicit about: several accessory circuits below are identical to Phase 1's (Day C's, in particular). That's intentional, not a copy-paste leftover - accessory work is meant to stay stable and supportive while the Strength Lane and Power Lane carry this phase's actual identity. Changing everything at once would make it harder to tell whether a training effect came from the new Power Lane work or from swapped-out accessories.

### Day A - Squat (Monday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints; no lateral bound this phase)
- Strength Lane: Back Squat. Ramp: 50% x5, 65% x3, 75% x2 (off the Phase 2 Testing Week e1RM). Work: 3 sets at the week's prescribed load and reps (Progression table below, % of e1RM). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
- Power Lane: Trap Bar Jump Squat, 5 sets x 3 reps at 30-40% of the Back Squat e1RM - light enough that speed, not load, is the point. Maximal intended bar speed on every rep, land soft, full reset between reps, rest 2 min between sets. (No trap bar: see Equipment Substitutions.)
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station unless noted): Split Squat, 10-12 reps per leg (COD/deceleration) · Plank/Core (30-45 sec hold) · Calf Raise
- **Post-session finisher:** Shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2 sets x 15-20 reps)

### Day B - Hinge (Tuesday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints; no lateral bound this phase)
- Strength Lane: Deadlift (alternate with Romanian Deadlift every other week, same rule as Phase 1 - RDL weeks use the prescribed % as a ceiling, not a target). Ramp: 50% x5, 65% x3, 75% x2 (off e1RM). Work: 3 sets at the week's prescribed load and reps (Progression table below). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
- Power Lane: Trap Bar Jump Shrug, 5 sets x 3 reps at 30-40% of the Deadlift e1RM - light enough that speed, not load, is the point, same logic as Day A's jump squat. Explosive hip-hinge-to-triple-extension, shrug and let the bar float, land soft, full reset between reps, rest 2 min between sets. No catch position to coach - that's the whole point of this substitution. (No trap bar: see Equipment Substitutions.)
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station unless noted): Overhead Press (dumbbell) · Pull-up or Band-Assisted Pull-up (same 8-12 rep, band-tension method as Phase 1) · Lateral Lunge, 10-12 reps per leg (COD) · Band Pallof Press, 10-12 reps per side
- **Post-session finisher:** Shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2 sets x 15-20 reps) **then** Nordic hamstring lower (2 sets x 8-10 reps; see Phase 1's Nordic section)

### Day C - Push (Thursday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints; no Nordic on this day)
- Strength Lane: Bench Press. Ramp: 50% x5, 65% x3, 75% x2 (off e1RM). Work: 3 sets at the week's prescribed load and reps (Progression table below). Rest 2-3 min between work sets.
- Power Lane: CAT Bench Press, 5 sets x 3 reps at 50-70% of the Bench e1RM. Maximal intended bar speed on the press, full range of motion, controlled on the way down - this is the exact method this phase's strongest football-specific evidence is built on, now correctly loaded against e1RM rather than a raw tested 5RM. Rest 2 min between sets.
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station unless noted): Front Squat or Goblet Squat (lighter, technique-focused) · Dumbbell Row · Walking Lunge, 10-12 reps per leg · Hanging Knee Raise, 10-15 reps (Reverse Crunch if no bar free)
- Shoulder-health finisher (2 sets x 15-20 reps)

### Day D - Pull / Rotational (Friday)

- NMT warm-up (trimmed: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints; Nordic runs post-session, see below)
- Strength Lane: same track logic as Phase 1's Day D - Weighted Pull-up track (technique-gated at 8+ bodyweight reps) or Bodyweight/Assisted track. Ramp and work sets follow the same structure as Phase 1's Day D, at the week's prescribed % of the total-system-load e1RM (bodyweight + added weight; belt/vest load = prescribed total - current bodyweight, zero if negative - see Phase 1's "Weighted pull-up: percentages apply to total load"). No back-off set this phase - the Power Lane below replaces it.
- Power Lane: Landmine Rotational Press or Medicine Ball Rotational Throw (pick one for the week, keep it consistent) - 4 sets x 5 reps per side, maximal explosive intent each rep, rest 90 sec between sets. This is the direct upgrade from Phase 1's Cable Woodchopper: same rotational pattern, now trained for power instead of just core stability.
- Accessory circuit (3 rounds, 12-15 reps/station unless noted): Overhead Press (barbell) - same tested-OHP-e1RM baseline as Phase 1's Day D, dosed as a true accessory rather than riding the Strength Lane's climbing weekly percentage: **3 sets x 5-8 reps at a flat 70-75% of the tested OHP e1RM, or RPE 7 - this percentage does not climb with the Strength Lane table and stays fixed all phase** · Single-leg Romanian Deadlift, 10-12 reps per leg · Step-up, 10-12 reps per leg · Side Plank, 30-45 sec each side
