Accessory weight selection: same found-weight method as Phase 1 - pick a weight landing 2-3 reps in reserve on the last set of 12-15, add weight once it feels clearly easy. Not repeated in full detail here; see the Phase 1 document.

## Multi-Sport Maintenance Track

Same purpose as Phase 1's version of this track - spring sports (track, baseball, softball, lacrosse, tennis, and others) run through this phase's entire window, and an athlete playing one of them can't reliably make 4 lifting days a week. This is a 2-day/week compressed version of the same program, at the same intensity, not a lighter substitute.

**Who uses it, and what stays unchanged:** same rules as Phase 1 - coach judgment based on real schedule conflicts, athletes move between tracks as their other sport's demands change, and the trimmed NMT warm-up (including the neck block), the Nordic hamstring lower and the shoulder-health finisher all continue as prescribed on the full track - none of that is cut (Nordic on Track Day 2 always, and on Track Day 1 only if the two track days are 48+ hours apart). The prerequisite gate on loaded jump-family work applies here too.

**What's different from Phase 1's version:** Phase 2's Strength Lane is already just 3 work sets (not 4), so there's no further per-session set trim here - the volume reduction comes entirely from cutting from 4 training days to 2 and dropping the accessory circuit, which is already a substantial cut (roughly half the weekly session count, plus ~15 minutes of accessory work removed from each remaining session). The Power Lane (CAT, jump-family work) stays at its full 5x3 dose on both track days - it's brief, high-value, and specifically the stimulus this phase exists to add, so it isn't the piece to cut.

**Track Day 1 — Squat + Push:**

- NMT warm-up (trimmed form: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints)
- Strength Lane: Back Squat, ramp + 3 sets at the week's prescribed load/reps (Progression table below)
- Power Lane: Trap Bar Jump Squat, 5x3 @ 30-40% Back Squat e1RM (or the unloaded gate option)
- Strength Lane: Bench Press, ramp + 3 sets at the week's prescribed load/reps
- Power Lane: CAT Bench Press, 5x3 @ that week's % of Bench e1RM (Progression table below)
- Post-session finisher: shoulder-health work (2x15-20), **then 2 sets x 10-12 reps light dumbbell Overhead Press, found-weight and submaximal (see What's dropped, below)**, then Nordic hamstring lower only if the two track days are 48+ hours apart

**Track Day 2 — Hinge + Pull:**

- NMT warm-up (trimmed form: Part 2 plus 2 build-up sprints)
- Strength Lane: Deadlift (alternate with Romanian Deadlift, same rule as the full track), ramp + 3 sets at the week's prescribed load/reps
- Power Lane: Trap Bar Jump Shrug, 5x3 @ 30-40% Deadlift e1RM (or the unloaded gate option)
- Strength Lane: Pull-up, same track logic as the full program's Day D
- Post-session finisher: shoulder-health work (2x15-20) then Nordic hamstring lower

**What's dropped:** the accessory circuit entirely (same as Phase 1's track), and Day D's Landmine Rotational Press/Medicine Ball Rotational Throw and Overhead Press accessory - there's no slot for them in a 2-lift-per-day session without pushing session length past what a time-crunched two-sport athlete can realistically fit. Overhead Press is still tested at Testing Week and the Week 7 retest if the athlete can make that session. Track Day 1's post-session finisher includes 2 sets x 10-12 reps of light, submaximal dumbbell Overhead Press - not a loading stimulus, just enough to keep overhead pressing capacity from going completely untrained for the whole phase. The week immediately before the Week 7 retest, Track Day 1's finisher swaps the dumbbell touch for 2 sets x 5 reps of barbell Overhead Press at a found, clearly submaximal weight (RPE 5-6 - Rating of Perceived Exertion, a 1-10 effort scale) - a technique re-acquaintance rep under the actual bar this athlete tests with, so the retest isn't the first loaded barbell-overhead rep since Testing Week.

**Session length:** roughly 55-65 minutes per day (~7 min NMT, two Strength Lane + Power Lane pairs at ~20-25 min each, ~2-4 min finisher) - longer than Phase 1's version since each day now carries two full Strength+Power pairs, but still well under the full track's two-separate-sessions time cost, and with half the weekly day count.

## Phase 2–3 Bridge (Closing the Testing Window Transition Gap)

This phase closes Friday, May 21, 2027, and Phase 3's Testing Window doesn't open until Monday, June 21 - roughly four and a half calendar weeks - with no structured session in that span if this bridge didn't exist - well past the roughly-a-week threshold where the transition-period guidance (capped volume/intensity for the first 7-10 days, a minimum of 4 non-maximal workouts before max-effort testing) applies. **The Multi-Sport Maintenance Track (above) continues, unchanged, from the first Tuesday after this phase closes (May 25) through Tuesday, June 15 (the last full school day; June 16 and 17 are single-session days).**

**What this bridge is for, and what it isn't.** This isn't a strength-building claim - it's a safety measure: going into a max-effort sprint/shuttle testing and the start of a higher-intensity field phase after four and a half weeks with zero structured training carries real soft-tissue-injury risk. The bridge closes that cold-start gap before the max-effort retest, using the same maintenance dose already behind the Multi-Sport Track.

**Who this applies to, and how.** Same population and same voluntary/coach-judgment basis as the Multi-Sport Track above - this isn't a mandatory extra commitment layered onto a roster already juggling spring-sport seasons and, by late May, finals and end-of-year school demands. An athlete who can make it continues the existing 2-day/week Track Day 1 (Squat + Push) / Track Day 2 (Hinge + Pull) structure exactly as written, at the same intensity, with the same NMT warm-up, Nordic hamstring lower, and shoulder-health finisher - nothing new to coach, nothing new to program. Spring-sport athletes already on this track through the regular season simply keep going; athletes who were on the full 4-day track return to this 2-day version once their own spring-sport season or end-of-year schedule makes 4 days impractical, which for most of the roster is effectively immediately, given finals and spring-sport playoffs typically land in this window.

**Dates.** A Monday/Thursday pattern would put two of its seven sessions on dates that don't work: Monday, May 31 is Memorial Day (a confirmed closure), and Thursday, June 17 is DHS's graduation day and last day of school (a single-session day unworkable for mandatory athletic activity). The bridge instead runs a **Tuesday/Friday pattern**, which clears both: Tuesday, May 25 - Friday, May 28 - Tuesday, June 1 - Friday, June 4 - Tuesday, June 8 - Friday, June 11 - Tuesday, June 15, 2027.

Two of those seven dates (Friday, May 28 and Tuesday, June 1) are also on the district calendar's contingent "emergency day" list, and realistically won't run most years: May 28 only becomes a school day if the district uses all 5 of its budgeted emergency days (the rarest of the five contingent dates to actually trigger), and June 1 needs at least 4. **Treat the bridge as 5 confirmed sessions - May 25, June 4, June 8, June 11, and June 15 - with May 28 and June 1 as a bonus if that year's winter was bad enough to need them as make-up days, not something to plan attendance or loading around.**

The last confirmed session (Tuesday, June 15) leaves a short, unavoidable 6-day gap before Testing Window opens Monday, June 21 - no session is programmed in that window (Wednesday, June 16 is itself a single-session day districtwide, DMS's promotion ceremony; Thursday, June 17 is graduation/last day). That 6-day gap is the same order of magnitude as the single-missed-day gaps this program already treats as routine elsewhere, not a gap requiring its own transition-period guidance.

**Progression and loads, with a re-entry ramp on June 4.** The bridge's two most reliable sessions - May 25 and June 4 - are 10 days apart, since the two sessions in between (May 28, June 1) are contingent bonus dates that won't run most years. **Friday, June 4's Strength Lane runs at 78% e1RM x3, not 86%** - the same conservative-restart figure used elsewhere in this program after a real layoff. The Power Lane (CAT) stays at its prescribed 70% throughout. May 25 and every confirmed session from June 8 on hold at the full Week 11 numbers (86% e1RM x3, Strength Lane; 70% Bench e1RM, Power Lane) - this is a one-session dip at the point the internal gap actually falls, not a lowered bridge overall. If May 28 or June 1 do run in a given year, they also hold at the full Week 11 numbers.

# Phase 3 — Early Summer Program: Speed & Conditioning

*September 20, 2026 · Kenneth Quinones, Assistant Football Coach LB/RB, Dover High School*

This is the operational program for Phase 3 (Early Summer — Speed & Conditioning): exercises, distances, loads, and session structure for the phase.

## Overview

Dates. Anchored to Dover Public Schools' confirmed 2026-2027 district calendar. Testing Window runs **Monday, June 21 – Tuesday, June 22, 2027**, and Week 2 begins the following Monday, **June 28, 2027**, training weeks running Monday–Thursday from there. If July 4th (Independence Day) falls inside a training week, skip that day's session and shift the remaining sessions in that week back by a day rather than doubling up — moot for 2027 specifically (July 4, 2027 is a Sunday, outside any training week), but kept as a standing rule for other years. Total phase length: 4 weeks (Testing Window + Weeks 2–4).

Frequency and structure. A 4-day repeating cycle for the phase's actual training emphasis, not four training days: Day A (Acceleration & Sled), Day B (Tempo & Skills), Day C (Plyometrics & SIT Conditioning), and a built-in rest day. Layered on top of it, Day D (Maintenance Lift) runs once a week for upper-body strength retention. Across a full week that leaves one truly open day beyond Day D and the rest day — it stays unscheduled (full rest, or a coach-approved makeup session for anyone who missed a day that week, same missed-day policy as Phases 1–2). Weekday mapping: Monday = Day A, Tuesday = Day B, Wednesday = Day D, Thursday = Day C, Friday open.

Offense/defense practice days. The staff runs an offense/defense split alongside this program — 2 offense days (install/air work) and 2 defense days (7v7, intra-squad) each week, immediately after the lift/conditioning session with only a short break between them. That practice segment is scheduled and run by the football coaching staff; which day carries offense versus defense is assigned here: **Monday (Day A) and Thursday (Day C) run offense; Tuesday (Day B) and Wednesday (Day D) run defense.** Monday and Thursday are this phase's two heaviest sessions (heavy sled/max-velocity work and plyometrics/SIT conditioning, respectively), so they're paired with the lower-demand install/air work rather than 7v7. Tuesday and Wednesday are the lightest sessions in the cadence, so they absorb 7v7's higher cutting/change-of-direction demand instead. This puts the two defense (7v7) days back-to-back rather than spread through the week — coaching staff should watch cumulative lower-body/connective-tissue load across those two days. A 5-minute reactivation block (reactive shuffle-and-cut work, a mirror drill, a few deceleration reps) runs before the practice segment on Tuesday and Wednesday specifically, closing the gap between a fatigued lift/conditioning session and competitive cutting work with no re-warm-up in between.

Location. Outdoor field/track, not the weight room. True acceleration, max-velocity, and sled work need to happen on grass or track — treadmills and the stationary bike are fine for supplemental GPP conditioning pieces elsewhere in the program, but they don't substitute for on-field sprint work here.

Roster and coaching staff. This phase starts right as the roster and staff both grow for summer: expect high-20s to low-30s athletes (up to 40) and 4+ coaches, versus the 10–15 athletes/2 coaches of the school-year phases. The Weekly Template below is built around exactly this: 4 coaches, 4 position/speed-grouped squads. Equipment quantity assumed for the room-logistics math in this document: 2 sleds. If the actual count differs, scale the zone-swap math in the Weekly Template proportionally.

Session length. Roughly 60–75 minutes for Days A–C's lift/conditioning portion: 10 minutes NMT warm-up, 35–45 minutes of the day's primary work, remainder for cooldown and hydration. Day D (Maintenance Lift) is shorter — roughly 40–45 minutes — per the Weekly Template. The coaching staff's offense/defense practice segment (see above) follows immediately after — roughly 45 minutes, after a short break and with no separate warm-up before it — making the full on-field day closer to 95–110 minutes on Days A/B/C and 85–90 minutes on Day D. That practice segment happens on the same field in the same weather, so the Heat & Hydration Checklist below should be read as covering the whole day, not just the lift/conditioning portion — see that section for what changes.

NMT warm-up. Standing 3-part protocol (including the neck block), unchanged from Phase 1 — all three parts, every session in this phase (the trimmed lift-only form used in Phases 1, 2 and 5 does not apply here: this phase's sessions are field speed, plyometric and conditioning work). Full routine is in the Phase 1 document; not repeated here. **Nordic hamstring lower (revised Oct 21, 2026): 2 sets x 8-10 reps, twice a week — pre-session in the NMT on Day B, and post-lift on Day D; none on Day A or Day C.** Never on consecutive days and never more than 3 in any 7 days: Day B repeats every 4 days while Day D is Wednesday, so if the two land within 48 hours of each other in a given week, run only the first and skip the second. Same back-off rules as Phase 1 (more than mild next-day hamstring soreness, hamstring tightness while sprinting, or a visible drop in sprint speed → skip it, 1 set next time, athletic trainer if it persists). **Stop-and-hand-off rules (concussion, injury or illness, new or persistent pain) from the Phase 1 document apply in this phase unchanged.**

Heat and hydration. This phase runs through late June and July, materially hotter than Phases 1–2. NJSIAA's WBGT Heat Participation Policy applies year-round to practices, not just to camp's 14-day acclimatization window, so Phase 3's outdoor sessions are themselves subject to it. Every session should include mandatory water breaks between zones/stations (not just at the end) and ice/cold-towel access on the field regardless of reading; the WBGT reading itself determines whether the session runs as written or gets modified. Coaches should also follow Dover's own heat-safety policy for outdoor summer athletics where it's stricter than NJSIAA's floor.

**Heat & Hydration Checklist:**

Every time cap and break-frequency rule below covers the full on-field day — lift/conditioning plus the practice segment that follows it — not just the lift/conditioning portion in isolation. A Red-tier "cap at 1 hour," for example, means the whole day (including practice) fits inside that hour, not that the lift/conditioning portion gets capped while practice runs afterward uncapped. Pull a second WBGT reading before the practice segment starts if more than 30–45 minutes have passed since the pre-lift reading, since WBGT can shift meaningfully across a summer morning; the higher of the two readings governs the rest of the day.

- Before every outdoor session (Days A, B, C - Day D is indoors), take an **on-site WBGT reading with a scientifically reliable WBGT device** (a handheld meter). NJSIAA's Heat Participation Policy requires a reading on site 30 minutes before activity and at least every hour during it, taken by the athletic trainer or a designee/coach appointed by the AD, and recorded on the NJSIAA Heat Participation Policy Record Chart. A phone's stock "heat index" is not a substitute - it omits solar radiation, wind, and sun angle, which is exactly why the policy specifies WBGT. **A forecast or calculator reading (the NWS National Digital Forecast Database WBGT product, perryweather.com) is NOT a compliant substitute for the on-site reading** - it is modeled regional data that can't see this field's own microclimate, especially turf heat. Use it only to plan ahead and spot borderline days. **If no device is on site, the session is not policy-compliant as run:** ask the AD/athletic trainer to supply one before the first outdoor session (before June 21), and until then treat any day with a forecast WBGT of 80.0°F or higher as at least Orange-tier and move to indoor/modified work if the forecast is Red-tier or higher - that is risk reduction, not compliance. See the Research Report's Safety section for the full reasoning.
- **Green (under 80°F WBGT):** run the session as written. 3 water breaks/hour minimum, 3 min each, is the floor even on a Green day.
- **Yellow (80.0-85.0°F):** run as written, but a coach can shorten sled/sprint rep counts at their discretion for any athlete showing heat strain. 3 breaks/hour, 4 min each.
- **Orange (85.1-88.0°F):** cap the full on-field day (lift/conditioning plus the practice segment that follows it) at 2 hours total — the lift/conditioning portion alone is well under that, but the practice segment brings the full day close to it, so treat this tier as real on a hot day rather than assuming there's slack. 4 breaks/hour, 4 min each. No pads/helmets applicable here since this is conditioning, not padded practice.
- **Red (88.1-90.0°F):** cap the full on-field day at 1 hour — this will require shortening or cutting the practice segment, not just the lift/conditioning portion, since the lift/conditioning alone can already run close to that on a Days A/B/C session. No SIT conditioning or sled work (the policy's "no conditioning work" restriction applies directly to Day A's sled/sprint and Day C's SIT circuit) - **no conditioning of any kind that day: no tempo running, no sled, no SIT, no conditioning-style movement outdoors or indoors.** Lift and mobility work indoors only (the Day D-style maintenance lift, NMT/mobility), and cancel field work. If any outdoor activity does run at this tier, it stays inside the 1-hour cap with 20 min of distributed rest breaks across it.
- **Black (over 90°F):** no outdoor session. Move to Day D's indoor lift template if it's a lift day, or cancel/reschedule if it's a field day - do not substitute a shortened outdoor session.
- **Air quality (recommended, not an NJSIAA requirement):** the person taking the WBGT reading also checks the local AQI (AirNow.gov) before each outdoor session. When air quality is in the unhealthy range, the athletic trainer or head coach on site moves the work indoors, shortens it, or cancels it per Dover's and the district's guidance - this program doesn't set its own AQI thresholds. (EPA/AirNow activity guidance wasn't verified for this document.)
- Anyone showing dizziness, nausea, confusion, stopped sweating, or skin that's hot/dry rather than sweaty stops immediately, moves to shade/AC, and gets evaluated - these are exertional heat illness warning signs, not something to push through to finish a set.
- **Heat-emergency readiness (check before the first outdoor session of the phase, then confirm each session):**
  - **Shaded rest site** set up at the field for every session, so an athlete who needs to stop has somewhere to go that isn't the turf.
  - **Ice towels or ice-water spray bottles** on the field whenever the WBGT reading is above 85°F.
  - **Cold-water immersion (CWI) on site:** a tub or tarp with water below 60°F, reachable within 5-10 minutes of any athlete on the field. The NJSIAA CWI language, as read in the policy copy reviewed, applies at 80°F WBGT and above; this program's own minimum is to have it staged and reachable on every Orange-or-higher day (85.1°F and up) and to treat 80.0°F+ as the safer default. **Caveat:** the policy copy reviewed for this document was a 2023 third-party-hosted copy, so have the AD confirm the current wording and the exact trigger.
  - **"Cool first, transport second."** For a suspected exertional heat stroke (collapse, confusion, altered behavior, hot skin), with an athletic trainer on site, cooling starts immediately where the athlete is and transport follows once cooling is underway. With no athletic trainer on site, call 911 and begin cooling immediately and keep going for at least 20 minutes while EMS is on the way. Do not wait for EMS to start.
  - **The written Emergency Action Plan (EAP), including heat injury, is owned by the AD/athletic trainer, not by this document.** This checklist feeds into it and does not replace it. Every coach on the field should know who calls 911, where the cooling equipment is staged, and where EMS enters the field.

Nutrition and sleep. Same standards as Phases 1–2: protein intake in the 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day range, consistent sleep in the 8–10 hour range. Both matter more, not less, in the heat and volume of a summer conditioning phase.

Missed-day policy. Same as Phases 1–2: a missed day is made up on one of the week's open days at reduced volume (roughly 75% of the missed session), never stacked on top of the next scheduled day.

## Testing Window (Monday June 21 – Tuesday June 22, 2027)

Split across two days specifically to separate the maximal-velocity/neural testing from the lactate/conditioning testing — running both on the same day would let shuttle-run fatigue contaminate the sprint numbers that drive Day A's sled-load calibration (the same fatigue-order confound identified and fixed in Phase 2's testing sequence).

There's a training gap before this window every year. With Phase 2 anchored to real dates, it closes Friday, May 21, 2027 — roughly **four and a half** calendar weeks before this Testing Window opens June 21. On the current calendar, that's the default gap every returning athlete faces, well past the roughly-a-week threshold that triggers transition-period guidance: capped volume and intensity for the first 7–10 days, a minimum of 4 non-maximal workouts, rather than moving straight into max-effort testing. This gap is addressed with a programmed bridge, not an optional stopgap: Phase 2's Multi-Sport Maintenance Track continues, 2 days a week, on a Tuesday/Friday pattern from May 25 through June 15, 2027 (see that document's "Phase 2–3 Bridge" section for the full structure and which of those sessions are confirmed versus a weather-dependent bonus). That leaves a short **6-day gap** between June 15 and this Testing Window's June 21 open — the same order of magnitude as a single missed day elsewhere in this program. This applies to essentially the whole roster every year, so coaches should treat the bridge as the standard expectation, not a contingency. A spring-sport athlete whose own season runs into June, or anyone with a shorter or longer personal gap than four and a half weeks, still follows the same underlying rule individually — it's the trigger (a real gap, not a fixed calendar date) that matters, and Phase 2's bridge is built to be voluntary/coach-judgment based for exactly that reason (see that document).

**Sprint runway before any timed sprint (added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review).** Day T1's maximal 10m/20m and 40-yard attempts must not be an athlete's first meaningful sprint exposure after a gap. Phases 1 and 2 keep 2 build-up sprints in every lift warm-up, and the Phase 2-3 Bridge sessions carry the same prep, so most returning athletes arrive with some exposure. **Anyone who missed the Bridge, is a first-time athlete, or hasn't sprinted in the last 3 weeks completes a graded runway first:** after NMT, 4-6 progressive accelerations of 20-30 yards at about 60%, 75%, then 85% effort, walking back between reps, in at least one session before timing (two is better). The coach records **runway done: yes/no** next to the athlete's name on the Day T1 sheet; if no, the athlete runs the runway reps at T1 and the timed attempts wait for the first Day A (use the shortened catch-up protocol below). Separately, the sprint test (Day T1) and the 300-yard shuttle (Day T2) are consecutive days; for first-time athletes and anyone without a completed runway, move the shuttle to **Thursday June 24** so a rest day sits between the two maximal efforts (confirm with the AD that the extra slot is available).

Testing-day logistics. Squads aren't assigned until after the Testing Window (see Weekly Template), so both testing days run as one roster-wide rotation rather than fixed squad groups: 2 of the 4 coaches run the timing stations (the 10m/20m marks, or the shuttle clock), while the other 2 manage the queue — one athlete at the line at a time, the rest resting and waiting their turn — so the full-recovery interval between sprint attempts happens naturally rather than needing separate scheduling.

First-time athletes test at Day T1/T2 with everyone else: they attend like every returning athlete, getting real bodyweight, 10m/20m, 40-yard, and 300-yard shuttle numbers. Add a brief movement screen to Day T1, before the speed testing below — coach watches an unloaded bench-press pattern (push-up or empty-bar press), an unloaded pull pattern (bodyweight row or dead-hang), an unloaded overhead-press pattern (dowel or empty bar overhead), an unloaded bodyweight squat, and an RDL pattern with a dowel/empty bar — the same four-pattern screen Phase 1's Novice Track uses. This doesn't hold anyone out of Day T1/T2's speed and conditioning testing or Weeks 2-3's Day A-C training — those are bodyweight-relative or already technique-gated and don't need this. It only determines their Day D path for the first two weeks — see Day D below.

An athlete who arrives after Testing Window but before Week 2's Day D still needs a fallback — see the Staggered and Late Arrivals section below for the short bodyweight/10m-20m protocol that covers that case.

**Day T1 (Monday June 21) — Speed.**

1. NMT warm-up.
2. Bodyweight recorded for every athlete (drives Day A's %BW sled loading).
3. 10m/20m acceleration sprint test: hand-timed, one coach at the 10m mark and one at the 20m mark, stopwatch start on the athlete's first movement (no starting blocks or reaction cue — self-start, matching how the phase's own acceleration work is cued). 3 attempts per athlete, full recovery (3+ minutes) between attempts, best time at each split recorded. Same two timers should run both the test and the Week 4 retest for consistency.
4. 40-yard sprint: 2 attempts, full recovery between, best time recorded. This is the familiar football benchmark number for coaches and players; the 10m/20m splits above are what actually drives training decisions.

**Day T2 (Tuesday June 22) — Conditioning baseline.**

1. NMT warm-up.
2. 300-yard shuttle run (6 x 50-yard shuttles, standard football conditioning benchmark): timed, walk/jog recovery to the line between reps as is standard for the test. This sets the baseline SIT/conditioning capacity used to calibrate Day C's interval volume by squad.

How these numbers get used. Bodyweight sets Day A's sled load in pounds from the %BW progression in the Progression Scheme below. The 10m/20m splits and the 300-yard shuttle time are used to sort athletes into speed-matched training groups (see Weekly Template) so sprint and interval work happens against evenly matched partners rather than the fastest and slowest athletes on the roster paired together. The 40-yard time is recorded for the season-benchmark record but doesn't itself set any training parameter.

Retest. All four numbers (bodyweight, 10m/20m splits, 40-yard, 300-yard shuttle) are retested in Week 4, using the same two-day split and the same timers, in the Day A and Day C slots of that week (see Weekly Template, Week 4). The retest serves two purposes this phase, both different from Phases 1–2's retest: it regroups speed-matched training pods if anyone's grouping has shifted, and it produces the season-entry benchmark numbers that carry into Phase 4 and, eventually, camp — there's no %-of-retested-max training load to recalculate here the way there was for the strength phases, since sled loading stays bodyweight-relative throughout.

## Staggered and Late Arrivals

The first-time-athlete path above assumes arrival at or near the Testing Window. In practice, not everyone shows up then: some athletes arrive on vacation schedules and don't show until later in the summer; some join as late as September. This section is the explicit policy for that variance.

- **Arrives at Testing Window, June 21-22 (the normal case):** tests at Day T1/T2 with everyone else, per the First-time athletes note above - no separate handling needed.
- **Arrives after Testing Window but by Week 2's Day D (a short slip - missed Day T1/T2 but not by much):** doesn't have real bodyweight/10m-20m/shuttle numbers on file. Run a short catch-up protocol at the start of whichever Day A session they first attend - record bodyweight, run one round of 10m/20m acceleration sprints (2 attempts, full recovery, best time - a shortened version of Day T1's 3-attempt protocol, enough to sort into a speed-matched squad without turning a training day into a second max-effort testing day), and add the movement screen there too if they missed it at T1. The 40-yard sprint and 300-yard shuttle aren't caught up separately - the 40-yard "doesn't itself set any training parameter" per the note below Day T2, and the 300-yard shuttle gets its first real data point from that week's own Day C session. This doesn't hold anyone out of Weeks 2-3's Day A-C training - that content is bodyweight-relative or already technique-gated and doesn't need a prior baseline the way Day A's sled load does.
- **Arrives during Week 3, after missing Week 2's Day D:** the missed session is made up on one of that week's open days at reduced volume, per this phase's standard missed-day policy - run the Week 2 RPE-based technique work (all five patterns) as the makeup, then attempt Week 3's test only if that makeup session and the coach's movement screen both look clean. If not, the athlete simply repeats technique work and tests later, following the same Phase 4 fallback already built into the path above.
- **Arrives after Week 3's test cutoff but before Phase 3 ends (roughly the back half of the phase, into early July):** too late to test on this phase's calendar. Run the movement screen and as much of the Week 2/3 RPE-based technique work as remaining Day D sessions allow; the athlete tests at the first available Day D slot in Phase 4 (Week 1), same as a Phase-3 athlete who wasn't clean by Week 3. They also join Phase 3's remaining Day A/B/C sessions immediately (that content is bodyweight-relative and technique-gated, not dependent on time-in-phase) rather than waiting for a training block to restart.
- **Arrives after Phase 3 has already ended (an "August" arrival, into Phase 4's taper):** this is a materially different situation, not just a later version of the case above - see Phase 4's "Late-arriving first-time athletes" section for the standalone on-ramp this requires. It is not safe to fold this athlete directly into Phase 4's Week 1 as written: that week's heavy 90-100% BW sled work and %e1RM taper lift both assume a Phase 3 progression this athlete never ran.
- **Arrives after Phase 4 has already ended (a "September" arrival, into camp or the season itself):** see Phase 5's "First-time athletes arriving after the off-season program" section. This is the latest-entry case the program accounts for, and the honest framing is that an athlete joining this late enters the season without a real strength base - the program's job at that point is making sure they aren't loaded against a number that doesn't exist, not pretending a few catch-up sessions closes a six-month gap.

**Individual-exposure rule for late arrivals (added Oct 21, 2026 after a safety review).** A late arrival is not dropped into the squad's calendar week. Sled, sprint, bound and shuttle work is progressed by that athlete's own completed exposures, not by the date: the first Day A starts at the Week 2 load (50-60% BW, 4-6 x 10m) whatever week the squad is on; the athlete moves to the Week 3 load (80-90% BW) only after at least two clean sessions at the lighter load with sprint mechanics checked under the sled (posture, shin angle, no collapse). Maximal sprints, bounds and SIT/shuttle intervals follow the same rule - first exposures at roughly 70-80% effort and the Week 2 rep/set count, advancing only after two successful exposures. An athlete who missed the introductory sessions also runs the sprint runway (see the Testing Window) before any maximal sprint. This applies equally to the Phase 4 and Phase 5 on-ramps referred to below.

**Squat/Deadlift always defer to Phase 4, regardless of arrival timing within Phase 3.** None of the arrival scenarios above change this: Squat/Deadlift are never tested inside Phase 3 for any first-time athlete, on-time or late - they get RPE-based technique work at whatever Day D sessions the athlete's actual arrival date allows (compressed to however many sessions remain if arriving mid-phase), and test in Phase 4, Week 1 regardless. A late Phase 3 arrival simply means fewer than three technique sessions get banked before that test - the coach's technique-gated judgment (not the calendar) still governs whether that's enough, same as an on-time arrival.

## Weekly Template (Weeks 2–3; Week 4 detailed separately below)

Squad setup (done once, after the Testing Window). Split the roster into 4 squads of roughly 8–10 athletes, one squad per coach. Squads are built from the Day T1 10m/20m results so each squad has a similar internal speed spread — not fastest-squad-vs-slowest-squad, but each squad containing a comparable mix, so no squad's sled lane or sprint reps are bottlenecked by one athlete's pace. Position balance (linemen vs. skill positions) should also be spread across all 4 squads rather than clustered, since Day B's skills circuit and the position-bias additions below need each squad to run both position tracks.

### Day A — Acceleration & Sled

1. NMT warm-up (10 min, all three parts; no Nordic on this day).
2. Acceleration mechanics: ankle bounces in place (2x15), A-March (2x15m), A-Skip (2x15m), wall drill — 3-position acceleration posture (tall–fall–run), 3x5 sec per leg, falling starts 3x10m.
3. Sled pulls: see Progression Scheme for the week's %BW load and rep count. Full recovery between reps (2–3 min) — this is a maximal-quality neural day, not a conditioning day; reps should never feel rushed.
4. Unresisted acceleration sprints: 3x10–20m at max effort, no sled — run immediately after sled work each week, pairing resisted and unresisted acceleration in the same session.
5. Skill-position addition: after step 4, skill positions (WR/DB/RB) add 2x30–40m flying sprints (10m build-up into 20–30m at top speed) to get top-end-speed exposure the base acceleration work doesn't cover. Linemen's session ends at step 4 — their base acceleration work already caps out close to their actual game-speed ceiling.
6. **Post-session: shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2x15-20).** No Nordic on this day.

Day A room logistics (2 sleds, 4 squads, 4 coaches). NMT (step 1) runs as one shared whole-squad warm-up before the group splits. After that, split the field into two zones instead of four — two sleds create a real throughput bottleneck against a 30–40-athlete roster, the same kind of equipment-bound problem Phase 1's single cable machine created. Zone 1 (Sled) runs both sleds in parallel, supervised by 2 of the 4 coaches: athletes run sled pulls (step 3) immediately followed by unresisted acceleration sprints (step 4) in the same zone's open space, pairing resisted and unresisted work as intended. Zone 2 (Acceleration Mechanics) runs step 2's drill sequence, supervised by the other 2 coaches. Two squads start in each zone; athletes queue by squad for their turn on either sled, with the queue itself providing the full-recovery interval between reps. At the session's midpoint, the two zone groups swap. Skill positions run their flying-sprint addition (step 5) after their squad's Zone 1 turn, regardless of which zone they started in.

### Day B — Tempo & Skills

1. NMT warm-up.
2. Tempo runs: 6–8 x 100m at roughly 70–75% effort, walk-back recovery. Sub-maximal, aerobic-capacity work that builds a work-capacity base without the CNS strain of max-velocity or sled work — this is the phase's lowest-intensity day, deliberately placed between the two higher-CNS-demand days.
3. Skills circuit: change-of-direction and football-movement drills, 4 stations x 4 reps each — backpedal-to-drive-sprint (10m), lateral shuffle-to-sprint (10m), footwork ladder (in-in-out-out pattern, 2 passes), cone-to-cone 45-degree cut (2 cuts, 10m total).
4. Position bias: skill positions run all 4 skills-circuit stations at the full 4 reps. Linemen run the same 4 stations at 2 reps each, with the recovered time used for 2 additional reps of the backpedal-to-drive station specifically — the movement pattern closest to their actual position demands (pass-set, then drive).

Day B room logistics. No equipment bottleneck (no sled), so the tempo-run portion runs as one full-roster group. For the skills circuit, the 4 coaches each supervise one of the 4 stations as a fixed post; squads rotate through all 4 stations in sequence rather than coaches moving.

### Day D — Maintenance Lift (Wednesday)

A short, reduced-volume session — not a return to Phase 1–2 progressive overload — aimed at holding upper-body strength through a phase whose other three days don't touch it, calibrated against e1RM, plus a light lower-body maintenance touch for returning athletes.

1. NMT warm-up (10 min).
2. Bench Press: 3x5 @ ~80% of each athlete's most recently tested **e1RM** (Phase 2, Week 7 retest, converted from 5RM).
3. **Squat: 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM** — a light maintenance touch, returning athletes only. First-time athletes skip this and follow their own Goblet Squat/DB RDL technique track below instead.
4. Pull-up (weighted, if the athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 retest called for added load): 3x5 at ~80% of the **total-system-load** e1RM (belt/vest load = 80% x [(bodyweight + added weight at the Phase 2, Week 7 retest) ÷ 0.87] - current bodyweight, rounded to 2.5 lb; bodyweight only if that comes out at or below zero); bodyweight athletes run 3x5 with 2–3 reps in reserve — same technique-gating standard as Phase 1.
5. **Deadlift (or Trap Bar Deadlift/RDL, if technique or load management calls for it): 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM** — same light maintenance touch and reasoning as Squat above, returning athletes only.
6. Overhead Press: 3x5 @ ~80% of each athlete's most recently tested e1RM.
7. Rest 2–3 min between sets on Bench/Pull-up/OHP — heavier load than a hypertrophy accessory set, so full recovery matters. The Squat/Deadlift maintenance touch, at only ~60% e1RM, needs less — 90 sec is enough. Controlled tempo, non-failure on every set.
8. **Post-lift finisher:** shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2x15–20) **then** Nordic hamstring lower (2 sets x 8-10 reps).

**First-time athletes:** a different path, since Day D only runs twice in this whole phase for the upper-body lifts (Weeks 2 and 3; Week 4's Wednesday adds only a third Squat/Deadlift technique session for first-timers - see Week 4 below) and there's no e1RM to load percentages against yet.

Squat and Deadlift also need a technique-and-test track for first-time athletes, separate from the returning-athlete maintenance touch above. A parallel Squat/RDL track is dosed lighter than the Bench/Pull-up/OHP work, since sled pulls and the plyometric circuit already give this population real lower-body loading elsewhere in the week — this track only needs to bank clean technique, not add a training stimulus.

Squat/Deadlift get three technique sessions before any 5RM test — not two — matching Phase 1's own 3-week technique-gated floor for the same movements (squat, hinge), which exists because of axial spinal loading and valgus/flexion risk under a raw beginner's still-developing stabilization. Bench/Pull-up/OHP keep a two-session runway, since there's no comparable axial-loading risk in those patterns. Squat/Deadlift are not tested at Week 4 — see below.

- **Week 2 Day D:** skip steps 2-6 above. Instead, RPE-based technique work at five patterns: Dumbbell Bench Press, Inverted Row (barbell racked at hip height in a squat rack, same setup as Phase 1's pull-up substitute) or band-assisted row, and Dumbbell Overhead Press - 3 sets x 8-10 reps each, RPE 6-7 (Rating of Perceived Exertion, a 1-10 effort scale - RPE 6-7 means 3-4 reps in reserve), same rest structure as Phase 1's Novice Track. Add Goblet Squat and Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift - 2 sets x 8-10 reps each, RPE 6 (lighter dose than the upper-body work; this is a technique bank, not a stimulus, given Days A/C already load the lower body this week).
- **Week 3 Day D:** if the coach's movement screen and Week 2's session both looked clean (full range of motion, no significant compensation) on the upper-body three, test a real 5RM on Bench Press, Pull-up (or the bodyweight/assisted branch, same rules as Phase 1's Testing Week), and Overhead Press - this session's Day D slot becomes a testing day for those three. Convert each to e1RM (÷0.87) immediately. If not yet clean, repeat Week 2's RPE-based work on the upper-body three instead of testing them - an athlete not ready by Week 3 tests them at the first available Day D slot in Phase 4 instead (see that document), which runs that week's Day D as a technique check plus test rather than a taper session. **Squat and Deadlift are never tested this session, regardless of how the upper-body three go** - run a second RPE 7 technique dose on Goblet Squat and DB Romanian Deadlift instead (2x8-10), banking session 2 of 3 before those two ever see a loaded test.
- **Week 4, Wednesday (uses the day that's otherwise open/rest for the main roster — see Weekly Template, Week 4):** a third RPE-based technique session on Goblet Squat and DB Romanian Deadlift (2x8-10, RPE 7) — still not a test. Three technique sessions are banked (Weeks 2, 3, and this one) before Squat/Deadlift ever go under a loaded 5RM, matching the floor Phase 1's Novice Track sets for the same movements.
- **Squat/Deadlift 5RM test runs in Phase 4, Week 1's Day D** (see that document) — a small-group addition to the returning roster's regular Day D session, run alongside (not instead of) their %e1RM taper lift. Convert each to e1RM immediately on testing. If the coach's judgment says three sessions still isn't clean technique, this is technique-gated the same way Phase 1's track is — not a calendar deadline: repeat the RPE work at Phase 4's Day D slots instead of testing, and push the test to the first clean opportunity, same principle Phase 1 uses ("a floor, not a ceiling").
- A first-time athlete who clears everything on schedule tests Squat/Deadlift the same week as Phase 4's Week 1, with the first post-test session following in Phase 4's Week 2 (a light Goblet Squat/DB RDL touch, not a barbell %e1RM session — see that document's Day D). This athlete therefore enters Phase 5's GD-4 (Squat) and GD-2 (Deadlift) with one 5RM test and one light touch behind them for each lift, and no barbell %e1RM training session — thinner than a returning athlete's training history by a wide margin, worth the coaching staff knowing going in.

Total session length: roughly 40–45 minutes (up slightly from 35-40 with the Squat/Deadlift maintenance addition), still shorter than Days A–C, since there's no field warm-up beyond NMT. The two added exercises run light and fast (~60% e1RM, 90 sec rest).

Day D room logistics. Back in the weight room, using the same 3–4 squat racks (squat/bench) and pull-up bars as Phases 1–2 — but against summer roster numbers (30–40 athletes) rather than the school-year 10–15. **Five exercise-stations now (Squat, Bench, Pull-up, Deadlift, Overhead Press)** — Squat and Bench both run on the available squat racks (light Squat work doesn't need its own dedicated rack time), Deadlift runs on open floor space near the racks, Pull-up and Overhead Press as before. Squads rotate through all 5 stations in sequence, landing on whichever rack is open for Squat/Bench when it's their turn.

### Day C — Plyometrics & SIT Conditioning

1. NMT warm-up (all three parts; no Nordic on this day).
2. Plyometric circuit: box jump (4x5), standing broad jump (3x5), single-leg bound (3x5 per leg), lateral bound (3x6 per side).
3. SIT conditioning: repeated maximal-effort shuttle sprints in sets, not distance running. This is repeated-sprint-ability/lactate-tolerance work in the SIT (sprint interval training) format — not "special endurance" in the sprint-coaching sense of that term (which refers to longer near-maximal efforts, roughly 80m+), a label this document doesn't use for it. See Progression Scheme for the week's set/rep count; standard interval is a 20m-out-and-back shuttle sprint (40m total) at maximal effort, ~30 sec recovery between reps within a set, ~3 min recovery between sets. This exact format is what camp's end-of-practice conditioning runs on once two-a-days begin (see Phase 5's Camp Bridge section) — the same 20m shuttle, the same position bias (below), scaled to whatever time the practice window leaves that day rather than this table's fixed weekly set/rep count. Against the coaching staff's actual ~10-minute end-of-practice allotment (a typical figure, not a hard ceiling — practice has real slack against NJSIAA's 3-hour cap), this phase's own 2-set structure (30 sec/rep, ~3 min/set) runs at full prescribed volume for every position group, linemen included — Phase 5's Camp Bridge section has the worked timing.
4. Position bias: linemen get the prescribed rep count with recovery intervals extended by roughly 25% (higher body mass and mechanical/heat load per rep at equivalent effort); skill positions run the full prescribed volume and recovery as written.
5. **Post-session: shoulder-health work (face pull or band pull-apart, 2x15-20).** No Nordic on this day.

Day C room logistics. No sled/equipment bottleneck. Squads are grouped by their Day T2 300-yard shuttle time so each squad's shuttle-sprint sets run against evenly matched pace, and the 4 coaches each own one squad's pacing and rest-interval timing directly, cycling through the plyometric stations as a group before moving to the shuttle sets together.

### Rest/Recovery Day

No formal session. Optional light mobility work and NMT-only reinforcement for athletes who want it, coach-supervised but not mandatory.

## Week 4 — Retest Week

Same day-slot structure as Weeks 2–3, with Day A and Day C's slots repurposed for retesting rather than normal training content. Day B runs as a normal Tempo & Skills day, positioned as the recovery buffer between the two retest days.

Day A slot → Speed Retest. NMT warm-up, then the full Day T1 battery (bodyweight, 10m/20m splits, 40-yard sprint), same two timers, same protocol, no sled work this day.

Day B slot → normal Tempo & Skills, run at the volumes prescribed for Week 3 (no further progression this week — the point is recovery between retest days, not a new training stimulus).

Day C slot → Conditioning Retest. NMT warm-up, then the Day T2 300-yard shuttle test, same protocol.

No Day D this week for returning athletes — Wednesday stays open/rest between Monday's speed retest and Thursday's conditioning retest, rather than adding lift volume on top of a retest week. First-time athletes are the one exception: Wednesday is their third RPE 7 Goblet Squat/DB RDL technique session (2x8-10, not a test; see Day D).

Results from this week regroup speed-matched squads if needed and set the season-entry benchmark numbers that carry into Phase 4.

## Progression Scheme

Sled load (Day A), by %BW of the athlete's Testing Window bodyweight:

| Week | Sled load | Reps | Recovery between reps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 2 | 50–60% BW (light–moderate) | 4–6 x 10m | 2–3 min |
| Week 3 | 80–90% BW (moderate) | 4–5 x 10m | 2–3 min |
| Week 4 | No sled work (Retest Week — see Weekly Template) | — | — |

Week 3's 80–90% BW band is a moderate load; this phase's 4-week length doesn't allow a third training week to progress further before the retest. If Phase 3 is extended by repeating a training block, the added week should progress to 90–100% BW, 3 x 10m (the same ceiling Phase 4's Week 1 uses) — appropriate once athletes have two weeks of technique under load already banked.

SIT conditioning (Day C):

| Week | Sets x reps | Distance | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 2 | 2 sets x 4 reps | 20m out-and-back (40m total) | 30 sec between reps, 3 min between sets |
| Week 3 | 2 sets x 5 reps | 20m out-and-back (40m total) | 30 sec between reps, 3 min between sets |
| Week 4 | Retest Week — no SIT conditioning this week | — | — |

Tempo and skills volume (Day B) stays constant across Weeks 2–4 (6–8 x 100m tempo runs; 4-station skills circuit at the reps specified in the Weekly Template) — this day is the phase's aerobic-base and technical-skill work, not a progressive-overload day, so it doesn't need a week-to-week climb.

Plyometric volume (Day C) also stays flat across Weeks 2-3 (Week 4's Day C slot is the conditioning retest), for a similar reason to Day B. Box height, broad-jump distance, and bounding distance are technique-gated here, not volume-gated — raise box height only once landings are quiet and controlled, the same standard Phase 1 uses — and at 4x5/3x5/3x6, this circuit is already conservative by adolescent plyometric-dosing standards. Unlike Day A's sled load, which progresses against a specific %BW target, there isn't a comparably specific week-by-week plyometric progression scheme for a block this short (4 weeks); landing quality and full recovery between reps, not rep/set climbs, are the actual progression variable here.

Maintenance lift (Day D) stays flat across Weeks 2–3 — 3x5 at ~80% of each athlete's most recently tested e1RM (bench, OHP) or equivalent relative intensity for pull-up, same every week: hold intensity, keep volume low, don't chase progression. **Squat and Deadlift's light maintenance touch (returning athletes only) also stays flat across Weeks 2-3 — 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM, same every week** — deliberately lighter than the Bench/OHP/Pull-up dose, since the goal is motor-pattern retention (sled work and plyometrics already load the lower body elsewhere this week), not strength retention. No Day D runs during the Testing Window or Week 4 (see Weekly Template, Week 4).

Auto-regulation. If an athlete's sled-pull technique breaks down under the prescribed load (hips rising, loss of forward lean, shortened stride), drop the load 5–10% rather than grinding the rep. Same principle applies to Day D's barbell work — drop the load before grinding a rep or letting technique break down — the same standard used across Phases 1–2's lifts, applied here to loaded sprint mechanics and Day D's reduced-volume lifting alike.

## Equipment Substitutions

| Called for | If unavailable, substitute |
| --- | --- |
| Weighted sled (2 units) | Partner-resisted sprints (a training partner holds a resistance band/harness from behind) or, if no sled or band is available, unresisted sprints at the same distances. **Do not substitute a weighted vest to approximate these %BW sled loads** - a vest is not a safe stand-in at these loads. |
| Second stopwatch/timer for split timing | Single-timer protocol: time the full 20m only, average 3 attempts, and use that average to estimate the 10m split proportionally rather than measuring it directly |
| Marked outdoor track | Any flat, safe grass or turf field surface, with distances measured and marked by cones or field paint |
| Footwork/agility ladder | Cone-only pattern drills covering the same in-in-out-out footwork sequence |
| Ice machine for hydration station | Coolers with bagged ice and cups; same water-break frequency and standing heat-day protocol from the Overview still applies regardless of ice source |

# Phase 4 — Pre-Camp Taper

*September 20, 2026 · Kenneth Quinones, Assistant Football Coach LB/RB, Dover High School*

## Overview

Dates. Phase 4 begins the Monday immediately following Phase 3's Week 4 retest. Phase 3's whole roster tests June 21-22, 2027 (June 17 is DHS's graduation day and last day of school, not a workable day to run roster-wide testing). Using Phase 3's dates (Testing Window Mon June 21 – Tue June 22, 2027; Weeks 2–4 running Monday–Thursday from June 28), Phase 3's Week 4 retest runs Monday, July 12 – Thursday, July 15, 2027. Phase 4's Week 1 begins Monday, July 19, 2027, and Week 2 ends Thursday, July 29, 2027 — leaving roughly 4 days of runway before the estimated blackout-week start (~Monday, August 2, 2027).

If there's a gap before Week 1 begins. If the actual 2027 calendar shifts Phase 3's end date earlier than planned, don't start this phase's heavy Week 1, Day A session cold off an unplanned break — apply the same transition-period guidance used everywhere else in this program: a few lighter acclimation touches (NMT, easy tempo, no sled or maximal sprinting) before resuming the normal schedule, rather than walking straight into a 90–100% BW sled session after a week of no coached training.

Frequency and structure. Weekday cadence is unchanged from Phase 3: Monday = Day A, Tuesday = Day B, Wednesday = Day D, Thursday = Day C, Friday open (unscheduled — full rest, or a coach-approved makeup session under the same missed-day policy as every other phase). The same 48+ hour CNS-recovery spacing this cadence exists to protect (Day A to Day C) matters even more in a phase built specifically around managing fatigue, so it carries forward without modification. Two distinct weeks run inside that same cadence: Week 1 (quality/transition) and Week 2 (deep taper/unload) — see Weekly Template.

Offense/defense practice days carry forward unchanged from Phase 3: Monday (Day A) and Thursday (Day C) run offense (install/air); Tuesday (Day B) and Wednesday (Day D) run defense (7v7). Keeping 7v7's cutting/change-of-direction demand off Monday's heavy sled work and Thursday's plyometric/conditioning work (this phase's two hardest sessions) protects the taper's own logic. The same 5-minute reactivation block used in Phase 3 (reactive shuffle-and-cut work, a mirror drill, a few deceleration reps) runs before defense-day practice on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Location. Same as Phase 3: outdoor field/track for Days A–C, weight room for Day D.

Roster, coaching staff, and squads. Same as Phase 3 — high-20s to low-30s athletes (up to 40), 4 coaches. Squads carry forward unchanged from Phase 3's speed-matched groupings; no new squad setup is needed. If the roster has changed materially over the gap between phases, coaches may re-sort using Phase 3's Week 4 10m/20m numbers, but no formal re-testing is programmed for this phase.

Room logistics. Unchanged in principle from Phase 3 — same squad-to-station rotation logic for Day A's sled zone, Day B's skills circuit, and Day D's now-5-exercise rotation (Squat, Bench, Pull-up, Deadlift, Overhead Press — see Phase 3 document for the detailed zone-rotation description; not repeated here). One change: this phase needs only 1 sled, not 2. Sled work appears exactly once across the entire phase (Week 1, Day A, 3 x 10m per athlete), so the throughput bottleneck that justified running 2 sleds in Phase 3 doesn't apply here.

Session length. Roughly 45–60 minutes for Days A–C's lift/conditioning portion in Week 1, shorter still in Week 2 (30–45 minutes) as volume drops: 10 minutes NMT warm-up, remainder for the day's now-reduced primary work plus cooldown/hydration. Day D runs roughly 40–45 minutes in Week 1 (up slightly from Phase 3's 35-40 following the Squat/Deadlift maintenance addition), shorter (30–35 minutes) in Week 2. The offense/defense practice segment follows immediately after, same as Phase 3 — roughly 45 minutes, after a short break plus the reactivation block on defense days, with no reduction between Week 1 and Week 2. That makes the full on-field day roughly 90–105 minutes on Days A/B/C in Week 1, narrowing to roughly 75–90 minutes in Week 2 as the lift/conditioning portion tapers while practice holds steady; Day D runs roughly 85–90 minutes in Week 1 and 75–80 minutes in Week 2 on the same logic. The Heat and hydration standard below (the same WBGT tiers as Phase 3) covers the whole day, same as Phase 3.

NMT warm-up, Nordic hamstring lower, and shoulder-health finisher. All three continue unchanged from Phase 3, at Phase 3's revised doses (Nordic 2 sets x 8-10, twice a week), in both weeks (NMT before every session, all three parts; the Nordic lower, 2 sets x 8-10, runs on Day B before the session and Day D after it only - the same twice-weekly rule as Phase 3, never on consecutive days - and none on Day A or C; the shoulder-health finisher stays after every session). Full protocols are in the Phase 1 document; not repeated here.

Heat and hydration. Same standard as Phase 3, if not more important: this phase runs through the hottest stretch of the summer, immediately before camp's own NJSIAA-mandated heat-acclimatization period begins. NJSIAA's WBGT Heat Participation Policy applies to this phase's own outdoor sessions directly (year-round, not camp-only) — use the same Green/Yellow/Orange/Red/Black checklist as Phase 3 (see that document for the full threshold table), taking an on-site WBGT reading with a device before Days A-C each session (30 minutes before and at least hourly; a forecast is not a substitute - see Phase 3). Mandatory water breaks between zones/stations and ice/cold-towel access on the field apply regardless of reading. This phase's own WBGT compliance doesn't substitute for camp's separate mandated 14-day acclimatization protocol — that's camp's responsibility, not this phase's — but arriving at camp from a phase that already ran hot sessions safely is exactly the preparation that mandate assumes. See Phase 5's Camp Bridge section for what resumes once camp begins, and when. As in Phase 3, every time cap in that checklist covers the whole on-field day — lift/conditioning plus the offense/defense practice segment that follows — not just the lift/conditioning portion. Given this phase's already-reduced session lengths, a Red or Black day here often means the practice segment gets cut short or cancelled outright, not just the lift. Red tier here means no conditioning at all (no tempo running, sled or SIT) - lift and mobility indoors only - and the Heat-emergency readiness items in Phase 3's checklist (shaded rest site, ice towels/spray above 85°F, CWI tub or tarp, "cool first, transport second," the AD/athletic trainer's written EAP) apply here unchanged. The recommended (not NJSIAA-required) AQI check from Phase 3 also applies, and so do the stop-and-hand-off rules from the Phase 1 document (concussion, injury or illness, new or persistent pain).

Nutrition and sleep. Same standards as every prior phase: protein intake in the 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day range, consistent sleep in the 8–10 hour range. Sleep in particular carries extra weight heading into camp, where the demands only increase.

Missed-day policy. Same as every prior phase: a missed day is made up on one of the week's open days at reduced volume (roughly 75% of the missed session), never stacked on top of the next scheduled day.

### Late-arriving first-time athletes

Late-arriving first-time athletes (see Phase 3's "Staggered and Late Arrivals" section for the full arrival-timeline policy). An athlete who joins after Phase 3 has already ended arrives with no e1RM on file and none of Phase 3's sled progression banked. They do not join Week 1's Day A or Day D as written — Week 1's 90-100% BW sled work and ~80% e1RM taper lift both assume a progression this athlete never ran, and starting a true beginner there is exactly the "move straight into max-effort testing off a real gap" scenario this program's transition-period guidance (used everywhere else in this program) exists to prevent.

Instead, this athlete runs a standalone on-ramp alongside the squad's normal Week 1/Week 2 sessions rather than inside them: NMT, the same acceleration-mechanics drills, sled work capped at Phase 3's Week 2 starting load (50-60% BW) rather than Phase 4's heavy tier, and Phase 3's first-time-athlete Day D technique content (Bench/Row/OHP plus Goblet Squat/DB RDL, RPE 6-7 — Rating of Perceived Exertion, a 1-10 effort scale) in place of the %e1RM taper lift. They also need an individual speed/conditioning baseline — bodyweight, 10m/20m splits, 300-yard shuttle — run on the open Friday slot or folded into an existing squad's testing rep, so Day A's %BW sled load has a real number once they do progress to it.

Testing follows Phase 3's revised, movement-specific runway (see that document's "Squat and Deadlift need a track here too"): Bench/Pull-up/OHP need one clean RPE 6-7 technique session before testing, but Squat/Deadlift need three — so this athlete's Bench/Pull-up/OHP test can land as early as Phase 4's Week 2, while Squat/Deadlift realistically doesn't clear until Phase 5's first week or later, once three technique touches (not two) are actually banked. Rushing that requirement to let a late arrival "catch up" defeats its purpose — a late arrival gets a longer runway from a later start, not a shorter one. At whichever point each movement group clears its own floor, this athlete runs the same "technique check plus test" Day D structure defined below, just shifted later.

Worth stating plainly: an athlete arriving this late enters camp and the season without a real strength base under them — a 1-2 week taper window doesn't close a gap Phases 1-3 were built to fill, and coaching staff should expect this athlete's overall readiness, not just their lift numbers, to lag entering camp.

## Weekly Template

### Week 1 — Day A: Heavy Sled & Speed (Quality)

1. NMT warm-up (10 min).
2. Acceleration mechanics, reduced volume: A-March (1x15m), A-Skip (1x15m), wall drill (2x5 sec per leg), falling starts (2x10m).
3. Sled pulls: 90–100% BW, 3 x 10m. Full recovery between reps (3+ min) — this is a single quality touch, not a volume session. %BW is a loading guideline, not a precise measure of actual resistance (surface, harness fit, and hardware all shift it) - confirm intensity by watching forward lean and stride length, not the number alone; drop load immediately if either degrades, from rep one.
4. Unresisted acceleration sprints: 2 x 10–20m at max effort, no sled.
5. Skill-position addition: 1 x 30m flying sprint (down from Phase 3's 2 x 30–40m) for top-end-speed maintenance. Linemen's session ends at step 4.

### Week 1 — Day B: Tempo & Skills (Reduced)

1. NMT warm-up.
2. Tempo runs: 4–5 x 100m at roughly 70–75% effort, walk-back recovery (down from Phase 3's 6–8 x 100m).
3. Skills circuit: same 4 stations as Phase 3, 2 reps each (down from 4).
4. Position bias: linemen run the same 4 stations at 1 rep each, with the time saved used for 1 additional backpedal-to-drive rep.

### Week 1 — Day C: Plyometrics & Conditioning (Reduced)

1. NMT warm-up.
2. Plyometric circuit, close to Phase 3 volume: box jump (3x5), standing broad jump (3x5), single-leg bound (2x5 per leg), lateral bound (2x6 per side).
3. SIT conditioning, cut hard: 1 set x 4 reps (down from Phase 3's 2 sets x 5 reps), same 20m out-and-back format, same recovery intervals.
4. Position bias: linemen keep the ~25% extended recovery interval on the SIT set, same as Phase 3.

### Week 1 — Day D: Maintenance Lift (Wednesday)

1. NMT warm-up (10 min).
2. Bench Press: 3x5 @ ~80% of each athlete's most recently tested **e1RM** (Phase 2, Week 7 retest) — unchanged from Phase 3.
3. **Squat: 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM** — the same light maintenance touch carried over from Phase 3's Day D, returning athletes only.
4. Pull-up (weighted, if applicable): 3x5 at ~80% of the **total-system-load** e1RM (belt/vest load = 80% x [(bodyweight + added weight at the Phase 2, Week 7 retest) ÷ 0.87] - current bodyweight, rounded to 2.5 lb; bodyweight only if that comes out at or below zero); bodyweight athletes run 3x5 with 2–3 reps in reserve.
5. **Deadlift (or Trap Bar Deadlift/RDL): 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM** — same maintenance touch and reasoning as Squat above.
6. Overhead Press: 3x5 @ ~80% of each athlete's most recently tested e1RM.
7. Rest 2–3 min between sets on Bench/Pull-up/OHP, controlled tempo, non-failure on every set. 90 sec is enough on the lighter Squat/Deadlift touch.

**First-time athletes: Squat/Deadlift 5RM test.** Phase 3 never tests Squat/Deadlift for a first-time athlete — it only banks three RPE 6-7 technique sessions on Goblet Squat/DB RDL (Weeks 2, 3, and 4) and hands off a technique-ready athlete. This session is where that test actually happens: every first-time athlete who banked those three sessions in Phase 3 tests Squat/Deadlift here, **in place of the returning-athlete maintenance-touch steps above (3 and 5)**, using the same 5RM protocol as every other tested lift in this program. This is the normal, expected path for every first-timer, not an exception.

**First-time athletes: Bench/Pull-up/OHP (a fallback, not the normal path).** A first-timer who tested Bench/Pull-up/OHP cleanly back in Phase 3's Week 3 does not repeat that test here. This fallback is only for an athlete who wasn't clean enough to clear it there — they run a technique check plus test on whichever of the upper-body three they haven't cleared yet, instead of those steps.

Keep each athlete to one movement group per session where possible (Squat/Deadlift, or the upper-body fallback) rather than testing five lifts in one day even at this point — the goal is a clean test, not a compressed one.

### Week 1 — Rest/Recovery Day

No formal session. Optional light mobility work and NMT-only reinforcement, coach-supervised but not mandatory.

### Week 2 — Day A: Speed Touch (No Sled)

1. NMT warm-up (10 min).
2. Acceleration mechanics, light: A-March (1x10m), wall drill (1x5 sec per leg).
3. Unresisted acceleration sprints only — no sled work this week: 2 x 10–15m at max effort, full recovery between reps.
4. Skill-position addition: 1 x 20–30m flying sprint touch. Linemen's session ends at step 3.

### Week 2 — Day B: Tempo & Skills (Light)

1. NMT warm-up.
2. Tempo runs: 3 x 100m at roughly 70% effort, walk-back recovery.
3. Skills circuit: same 4 stations, 1–2 reps each, walkthrough pace rather than full training speed — the point this week is movement quality, not conditioning stimulus.

### Week 2 — Day C: Plyometrics (Low Volume, No Conditioning)

1. NMT warm-up.
2. Plyometric circuit, low volume but full quality/intensity: box jump (2x3), standing broad jump (2x3), single-leg bound (1x5 per leg), lateral bound (1x6 per side). Fewer reps, same technique standard as every other phase — never rushed, never at less than full effort.
3. No SIT conditioning this week — dropped entirely.

### Week 2 — Day D: Taper Lift (Wednesday)

1. NMT warm-up (10 min).
2. Bench Press: 2x5 @ ~75% of each athlete's most recently tested **e1RM** (down from Week 1's 3x5 @ ~80%).
3. **Squat: 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM** (unchanged from Week 1 — already light enough that the taper trim doesn't apply), returning athletes only.
4. Pull-up (weighted, if applicable): 2x5 at ~75% of the total-system-load e1RM (same formula as Week 1; down from Week 1's 3x5 @ ~80%); bodyweight athletes run 2x5 with 2–3 reps in reserve.
5. **Deadlift (or Trap Bar Deadlift/RDL): 2x5 @ ~60% of each athlete's Phase 2, Week 7 e1RM** (unchanged from Week 1, same reasoning as Squat above).
6. Overhead Press: 2x5 @ ~75% of each athlete's most recently tested e1RM.

**First-time athletes who tested Squat/Deadlift in Week 1, Day D:** add Goblet Squat and DB RDL, 2x5 @ RPE 6, in place of the returning-athlete Squat/Deadlift touch above (steps 3 and 5). This is deliberately not a barbell %e1RM session — it's a second light touch on the same movement pattern, at the same submaximal load Phase 3 used to build the technique base in the first place, so this athlete doesn't go from a single Week 1 test straight into Phase 5's in-season GD-4/GD-2 work with nothing banked in between. **Returning athletes now carry their own Squat/Deadlift maintenance touch in both weeks** (steps 3 and 5 above) — this closes the gap where Phase 4's Day D previously carried nothing for them between Phase 2's close and Phase 5's opener.

### Week 2 — Rest/Recovery Day

No formal session. Optional light mobility work only — this is the week directly before blackout week, so err toward less rather than more.

## Progression Scheme

Sled load (Week 1, Day A only):

| Week | Sled load | Reps | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | 90–100% BW (heavy) | 3 x 10m | 3+ min |
| Week 2 | No sled work | — | — |

Load is calculated from each athlete's Week 4 retest bodyweight (Phase 3 document), the most current measurement on file, not the earlier Testing Window figure.

Volume compared against Phase 3's Week 3 baseline, by modality:

| Modality | Phase 3 Week 3 (baseline) | Phase 4 Week 1 | Phase 4 Week 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sled (Day A) | 4–5 x 10m @ 80–90% BW | 3 x 10m @ 90–100% BW | Dropped |
| Unresisted accel. sprints (Day A) | 3 x 10–20m | 2 x 10–20m | 2 x 10–15m |
| Tempo runs (Day B) | 6–8 x 100m | 4–5 x 100m | 3 x 100m |
| Skills circuit (Day B) | 4 stations x 4 reps | 4 stations x 2 reps | 4 stations x 1–2 reps (walkthrough pace) |
| Plyometric circuit (Day C) | 4x5 / 3x5 / 3x5 / 3x6 | 3x5 / 3x5 / 2x5 / 2x6 | 2x3 / 2x3 / 1x5 / 1x6 |
| SIT conditioning (Day C) | 2 sets x 5 reps | 1 set x 4 reps | Dropped |
| Day D lift | 3x5 @ ~80% tested e1RM | 3x5 @ ~80% tested e1RM (unchanged) | 2x5 @ ~75% tested e1RM |

Auto-regulation. If an athlete's sled technique breaks down under Week 1's heavy load (hips rising, loss of forward lean, shortened stride), drop the load 5–10% rather than grinding the rep — same standard as every prior phase. More broadly for this phase specifically: if an athlete looks flat, heavy-legged, or generally overreached at any point in Week 2, the correct adjustment is less volume, not more effort. The entire purpose of this phase is arriving at camp fresh; grinding through a taper defeats the point of running one.

## Equipment Substitutions

| Called for | If unavailable, substitute |
| --- | --- |
| Weighted sled (1 unit) | Partner-resisted sprints (a training partner holds a resistance band/harness from behind) or, if no sled or band is available, unresisted sprints at the same distances. **Do not substitute a weighted vest for the 90–100% BW sled load** - a vest is not a safe stand-in at that load. |
| Stopwatch/timer | Any phone or watch stopwatch function; single-timer protocol is sufficient since this phase runs no squad-wide split-timed testing (late-arriving first-timers' individual baseline is the one timed exception) |
| Marked outdoor track | Any flat, safe grass or turf field surface, with distances measured and marked by cones or field paint |
| Footwork/agility ladder | Cone-only pattern drills covering the same footwork sequence |
| Ice machine for hydration station | Coolers with bagged ice and cups; same water-break frequency and standing heat-day protocol from the Overview still applies regardless of ice source |
